publications.title: Vision Transformer Approaches for Diabetic Retinopathy
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Advances in Computation, Communication and Information Technology (ICAICCIT)
publications.abstract: The focus of this paper is to identify how deep learning can be utilised in identifying diabetic retinopathy, a serious complication of diabetes which causes blindness. In this paper, an end-to-end system is proposed for diagnosing the early signs of disease using CNN to analyze images. Cropped Retinal - CNN - Early Diagnosis of the First Stage of the Disease. The overall performance of the proposed system is determined using accuracy, precision, and usability that are far much better than the conventional method of diagnosing the syndromes. Five models are explored under this study which includes Vision Transformer (ViT), Convolutional Neural Network, MobileNetV2, YOLO and Hybrid model (ViT+CNN). five levels of Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) are explored viz., No, Mild, Moderate, Severe and Proliferative DR. From these five models, the hybrid model achieved a $\mathbf{9 4 \%}$ of accuracy on the DR dataset. More future work includes the expansion of the expressed model and the inclusion of real-time image processing for clinical use.

publications.title: Real World Autonomous IoT Based Data Privacy Protection Using Machine Learning
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Science Technology Engineering and Mathematics (ICONSTEM)
publications.abstract: Connecting everyday objects to the web (IoT)has rapidly grown what might be anticipated to continue expanding with an estimated By 2025, there will be 75 billion linked gadgets. This increase in IoT devices has led to concerns regarding data privacy and security. Autonomous IoT-based data privacy protection using machine learning (ML) has the potential to address these concerns.This research proposes a real-world application of autonomous IoT-based data privacy protection using ML. The system will use ML algorithms to analyze data and identify potential privacy breaches. It will then autonomously take appropriate actions to protect the data and prevent further breaches.The proposed research will use a mixed-methods approach, including surveys, case studies, and experiments, to collect data from IoT users, privacy experts, and ML researchers. The data collected will be used to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed system in protecting data privacy and to identify any potential ethical concerns.The expected outcomes of this research are the development of an autonomous IoT-based data privacy protection system using ML, evaluation of its effectiveness in protecting data privacy, and identification of any ethical concerns that may arise.Overall, this research has the potential to contribute to the development of autonomous IoT-based data privacy protection systems that are effective in protecting data privacy while upholding ethical standards. The proposed Ultimately, this strategy might significantly alter the status quo of data privacy is protected in IoT, ensuring that users can confidently use IoT devices without concerns about privacy breaches.

publications.title: A Hybrid 2D–3D Deep Learning Framework for Automated Intracranial Aneurysm Segmentation and Morphological Risk Stratification from TOF-MRA
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Control Systems (ICICCS)
publications.abstract: Intracranial aneurysm assessment from time-of-flight MR angiography (TOF-MRA) is clinically important, yet automated aneurysm-only segmentation remains challenging because aneurysms are often small, have weak boundaries, and lie adjacent to complex vascular structures. This paper presents a hybrid 2D-3D deep learning framework that performs volumetric aneurysm segmentation and then derives an interpretable morphology-based rupture-risk indicator from the predicted mask. The pipeline standardizes each TOF-MRA volume by resampling to$1 \times 1 \times 1 \text{mm} 3$isotropic spacing and applying robust intensity normalization using percentile clipping followed by z -score scaling. The segmentation model is optimized with a hybrid objective that combines Dice overlap and voxel-wise binary cross-entropy, enabling stable learning under severe foreground sparsity. Experiments on the Lausanne TOF-MRA dataset (284 volumes; train =200, test =84) demonstrate consistent segmentation performance (mean Dice =0.9326 ± 0.0284, Hausdorff distance =0.7185 ± 0.2743), with size-stratified analysis confirming robustness across small, medium, and large aneurysms. Overall, the proposed segmentation-to-morphology pipeline provides a practical route to aneurysm delineation and interpretable morphology-based risk scoring from TOF-MRA.

publications.title: A Real-Time Deep Learning System for Facial Emotion Estimation with Temporal Feature Fusion
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Networking and Communications (ICNWC)
publications.abstract: Facial Emotion Recognition (FER) in real-time video streams is difficult due to the need for high accuracy in the presence of pose, lighting, and occlusion changes, while at the same time, the FER system must process video at real-time rates. This paper proposes a deep visual intelligence system for estimating emotions using real-time video frames. The proposed system first detects faces and normalizes them using facial landmark detection. The system then uses an efficient Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to obtain a compact spatiotemporal representation of facial features. To improve the quality of features, the system uses a lightweight attention module called the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to focus on the most significant facial features for emotion prediction. The system aggregates features over a short window using a lightweight sequence model to reduce noise in facial feature prediction for each video frame, resulting in accurate emotion prediction. The system is tested using three popular datasets, namely, CK+, FER2013, and AffectNet, and achieves accuracy rates of 96.8%, 76.4%, and 61.3%, respectively, while maintaining a high rate of 30-32 frames per second, indicating the efficiency of the proposed deep visual intelligence system for real-time emotion prediction.

publications.title: A Transformer-Based Cross-Modal Framework for Clinically Faithful Medical Image Captioning
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Signal, Systems, and Computing for Next-Gen Automation (ICSSCNA)
publications.abstract: Radiology reporting from chest X-ray (CXR) images is a critical clinical task that requires both diagnostic precision and linguistic clarity. Although recent advances in automated medical image captioning have improved fluency, many existing systems continue to generate clinically unsupported or hallucinated findings. This paper presents a Transformer-based cross-modal framework designed to enhance clinical faithfulness in radiology report generation. A Vision Transformer (ViT) encodes global anatomical representations, while cross-modal attention mechanisms align visual features with textual tokens during decoding. To further reduce hallucinated findings, a lightweight clinical faithfulness module re-weights token probabilities using image-conditioned evidence. The proposed framework is evaluated on the MIMICCXR and IU X-Ray datasets. Experimental results demonstrate consistent improvements in BLEU, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, and clinical accuracy compared to a baseline Transformer model. The findings indicate that explicit visual grounding combined with faithfulness-aware decoding significantly improves diagnostic reliability in automated radiology reporting systems.

publications.title: AI-Driven Framework for Zero-Day Vulnerability Detection and Prevention in Application and Cloud Environments
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Control Systems (ICICCS)
publications.abstract: Zero-day vulnerabilities are difficult to identify in modern software systems because exploit triggers are often novel, semantics-aware, and spread across both application logic and cloud execution contexts. This paper proposes an AI-driven autonomous discovery framework that prioritizes zero-day detection while preserving high quality forensic evidence at the moment a fault is surfaced. The framework integrates a Deep Q-Network (DQN) agent to guide semantic input exploration with an instrumented execution harness that supports hybrid monitoring and crash-resilient evidence logging. The design enables consistent analysis across local applications and cloud-hosted services, allowing vulnerability signals to be captured from heterogeneous runtime behaviors. In the implementation, the autonomous discovery engine executed 268,435,456 cycles and revealed 13 distinct logic- and memory-related failure modes, including high-severity deserialization driven faults and deep semantic gate violations.

publications.title: Agentic LLM-Driven Cyber Threat Hunting Using MITRE ATT&CK Knowledge Mapping and Graph-Based Evidence Correlation
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Networking and Communications (ICNWC)
publications.abstract: Modern cyberattacks are increasingly utilizing multi-stage, evasive, and automated approaches that are difficult to detect with standard rule-based monitoring systems. Security analysts must study massive amounts of diverse security records, which makes manual correlation and threat detection time-consuming and error-prone. This study provides an Agentic Large Language Model (LLM)-based cyber threat hunting system that analyzes suspicious security activities using contextual reasoning and adaptive investigative tactics. The proposed system combines agentic planning with LLM-based analysis to generate investigation hypotheses, correlate multi-source security telemetry, and map detected behaviors to the MITRE ATT&CK knowledge framework for standardized threat classification. Graph-based evidence correlation is used to identify relationships between entities such as hosts, users, IP addresses, and domains, allowing detection of coordinated attack patterns.The methodology also incorporates IOC enrichment and adaptive risk assessment to aid in prioritized threat response and analyst decision-making.

publications.title: An AI-Driven Drift-Aware Framework for Cyber Threat Detection Using Cloud Log Analysis
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Control Systems (ICICCS)
publications.abstract: This involves volumes of security telemetry data being created from modern-day clouds and enterprise networks, where there is a need for timely analyses of generated data in relation to detecting potential cyber-attacks and managing false alarms. This research has proposed an end-to-end machine learning framework for detecting cyber threat patterns based on flow and log-based traffic data. Subsequently, an aggregated dataset of approximately 2.83 million samples is generated by combining eight traffic capture files. After pruning out invalid and incomplete data samples, an ultimately desired dataset of 2,827,876 samples with 78 numerical features remains. In this case, a gradient boost decision tree model has been used for binary classification between the two categories, “BENIGN” and “ATTACK,” to obtain an accuracy of up to 99.93%. Through assessing the model's performance using ROC analysis, it has been found that the AUC is equal to 1.00, while proper determination of the model's optimized threshold results in a true positive rate of up to 0.9999, along with a false positive rate of up to 0.0011. For classifying attack-related categories, a multi-class classification has used a gradient boost model, resulting in an accuracy of up to 99.9 % for categories that currently exist. An “Isolation Forest” method has also been used to identify unusual patterns that may indicate zero-day attack behavior, thereby improving robustness in real-world scenarios. Analysis of the results will probably show that the model developed by the proposed framework provides reliable and understandable results, extending its use to scenarios where conditions are rapidly changing.

publications.title: Design and Experimental Assessment of a Speed Breaker-Integrated Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting System
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Networking and Communications (ICNWC)
publications.abstract: Road traffic continuously dissipates mechanical energy as vehicles interact with road features such as speed breakers. This paper presents a compact piezoelectric energy-harvesting prototype in which a piezoelectric sensor array is embedded beneath a speed breaker plate to convert transient compressive stress into electrical energy. The harvested alternating voltage is conditioned using a bridge rectifier and smoothing capacitor, then routed to an energy-storage stage suitable for low-power roadside loads. A laboratory-scale prototype using a 3×3 PZT disc array demonstrates repeatable voltage generation under different equivalent loading levels. Measured results show that peak open-circuit voltage increases with load, while the usable energy delivered to a resistive load remains in the millijoule range for disc-type sensors, highlighting the importance of impedance matching, mechanical force distribution, and scalable modular deployment. The suggested design and working model will serve as a low-cost design to power ultra-low power devices (e.g. beacons, sensor nodes, and intermittent indicators) as well as future lane-scale integration with higher energy piezoelectric stacks and robust encapsulation.

publications.title: Design and performance evaluation of an energy-aware post-quantum cryptographic system with adaptive lattice–hash integration for secure IoT applications
publications.journalOrConferenceName: Engineering Science and Technology an International Journal
publications.abstract: Post-quantum secure communication solutions are needed in engineering areas with distributed, resource-constrained infrastructures, such as Internet of Things (IoT) networks, due to the rapid expansion of quantum computing. The practical deployment of quantum-resistant cryptographic techniques is limited by computing cost, energy inefficiency, and implementation-level side-channel vulnerabilities. Lattice-based and hash-based post-quantum cryptography systems exhibit significant execution latency, large memory footprints, and poor adaptability to diverse device settings. Lack of system-level optimization and adaptive cryptographic selection limits their use in real-time engineering systems, where energy-performance trade-offs and secure execution are crucial. This study offers an adaptive, energy-aware Hybrid Quantum-Resistant Security Framework (HQR-SF) that combines lattice-based key encapsulation with hash-based digital signature techniques to overcome these issues. The HQR-SF’s context-driven cryptographic selection engine configures security primitives depending on anticipated threat level, computing capability, and data sensitivity. A constant-time vectorized polynomial transformation module accelerates modular arithmetic while reducing timing and power-based side-channel leakage. In the case of limited engineering systems, the framework offers a secure end-to-end communication path, complete with hybrid key exchange, authentication and data integrity protection enforcement. The proposed HQR-SF is evaluated within a testbed, which is developed through a simulation, to represent operational constraints of IoT, such as processor capacity and energy limitations. Experimental results reveal that, with a security score of 98.6%, HQR-SF reduces latency, memory consumption, computational cost, communication overhead and energy consumption by 35.93%, 25.64%, 34.55%, 17.65% and 20.10% respectively compared to the baseline approach. The framework is also easily extensible to address a variety of device types and is appropriate for use in future secure engineering infrastructures with scale.

publications.title: GAN-Based Lung X-Ray Image Enhancement and Denoising
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Signal, Systems, and Computing for Next-Gen Automation (ICSSCNA)
publications.abstract: Chest X-ray (CXR) is also extensively employed to assess the state of the lungs and track the development of the diseases. Nevertheless, they may be impaired by noise, low contrast, and acquisition-related degradations that may diminish the quality of the diagnostic data and blur the imaging of the minor anatomical structures. The paper presents a conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN) as a suggestion to improve and denoise lung X-ray images. The methodology is founded on the Pix2Pix framework, which relates to the usage of a U-Net generator and a conditional PatchGAN discriminator to be trained in such a way that it learns a mapping between noisy chest radiographs and clean target images. Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) are used as the model performance. On the test set, it has been experimentally found that the mean PSNR is 11.57 dB and the mean SSIM is 0.6933. The qualitative analysis shows that the model has a positive effect on minimizing noise and maintaining major thoracic structures. But a little-bit sharpening of small features indicates the usual trade-off between denoising and sharpness. On the whole, the given approach offers a viable GAN-based baseline CXR enhancement and reflects the prospects of its further advancement.

publications.title: Grad-CAM Integrated CNN for Explainable Brain Tumor Classification and Localization
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Signal, Systems, and Computing for Next-Gen Automation (ICSSCNA)
publications.abstract: The classification of brain tumors using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) does not just need a high predictive accuracy but also must be visually interpretable due to clinical decision-making support requests for deep learning models. This paper illustrates a Grad-CAM based explainable convolutional neural network framework for brain tumor classification and localization from MRI scans. The suggested model operates as a unified pipeline, where multiclass prediction and spatial explanation are both derived from the same learned feature representation. A specially made residual CNN combined with squeeze-and-excitation attention was used to classify the MRI images into glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, and no-tumor. The Brain Tumor MRI Dataset was the training dataset used for CNN model training with weighted cross-entropy, Adam optimizer, learning-rate scheduling, and early stopping. From experimental evaluation it was proved that the framework achieved a test accuracy of 97.18 %. Furthermore, it achieved strong class-wise precision, recall, F1-score values. The one-vsrest ROC analysis achieved an AUC of 0.97 for glioma, 0.96 for meningioma, and 0.99 for no-tumor/pituitary, confirming its excellent class discrimination. The Grad-CAM visualizations also highlighted the lesion-relevant areas in the correctly predicted MRI scans apart from classification which affirms the decision was guided by the image. The results show that the structure achieves a good compromise level between predictive performance and interpretability. Thus, it shows promise for an explainable computer-aided brain tumor analysis from MRI data.

publications.title: Intelligent Multi-Layer Penetration Testing System using Hybrid AI Models
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Smart Electronic Devices and Intelligent Systems (ICSEDIS)
publications.abstract: Due to today’s adversarial computing landscape, continuous and scalable security assessment is needed. However, penetration testing still suffers from primarily a highly manual effort emerged from exist complimentary yet disjointed tools. The capabilities of penetration testers are outstripped by the threat landscape and full testing is lagging on completion. To overcome these limitations, this paper presents an Intelligent Multi-Layer Penetration Testing System that integrates different artificial intelligence procedures within a single architecture to automate and speed up the end-to-end penetration testing process. In particular, the framework uses a supervised machine learning classifier obviously, which is Random Forest. In addition to that, it uses a deep learning sequence prediction model, which is Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory. Furthermore, it uses a deep reinforcement learning agent which is Deep Q-Network. Most importantly, it helps to model hypotheses, map attack steps, plan and learn inside a constrained network of pen-testing tools. An assessment conducted on a validated virtualisation-enabled testbed of a large enterprise network demonstrates that the system achieves a classification accuracy of 97.5% and an F1-score of 97.4%. Moreover, the system substantially outperforms Q-learning as well as deep reinforcement learning baselines. End-to-end estimation requires 20 hours of time as compared to 160 hours of time needed for manual testing. Many strict controls on access and data validation ensure non-destructive verification and suitability to an authorized security assessment and academic research environments.

publications.title: Lung X-Ray Based Disease Classification Using Deep Learning
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference Trends Material Science and Inventive Materials
publications.abstract: This work proposes a deep learning framework for multi-label recognition of thoracic diseases from chest X-ray images in practical conditions where a single radiograph may contain multiple co-existing findings. Using the NIH ChestXray14 dataset (86,524 images for training/validation and 25,596 for testing), we build a transfer-learning model based on DenseNet121 pretrained on ImageNet. Images are resized to$224 \times 224$and normalized, with lightweight augmentation (rotation, zoom, horizontal flip) applied during training. To reduce the dominance of normal scans, the “No Finding” class is down sampled (12,000 normal vs. 30,620 diseased samples) before optimization. The network is trained with Adam ($1 \mathrm{e}-4$) using sigmoid outputs and binary cross-entropy, and all training/inference runs are executed on a CUDA-enabled NVIDIA GPU for accelerated computation. On the held-out test set, the model achieves a mean ROC-AUC of 0.790 across 15 labels (14 diseases + No Finding), with strong AUCs for Emphysema (0.910), Hernia (0.886), Cardiomegaly (0.874), and Pneumothorax (0.866). The overall labelwise accuracy reaches 0.897, indicating reliable perlabel discrimination despite class imbalance. Performance drops for visually diffuse or label-noisy conditions (e.g., Infiltration), motivating future work on class-specific thresholds, calibration, and imbalance-aware losses to further improve recall on rare findings.

publications.title: MuFiTwin-Opt for Energy-Aware VM Migration in Heterogeneous Cloud Data Centers
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference Trends Material Science and Inventive Materials
publications.abstract: Live virtual machine migration is a technique in managing cloud resources. It helps to balance workloads and keep system performance good. Many current methods mostly use simulation results and do not think about real-world platform limits like bandwidth issues, migration time and different system setups. Also decisions on migration and placement are often made separately which can make things less efficient in changing environments. To solve these problems we introduce the MuFiTwin-Opt framework. It is designed for virtual machine migration in cloud data centers with different setups keeping in mind service level agreements. This framework is designed for an affordable solution and deals with any cloud in real-time. It adopts a simulation approach that is neither too detailed nor too simplistic. This approach examines migration possibilities and then considers numerous elements, including energy consumption, the frequency of migrations, and SLA violations. By considering these factors when making decisions the MuFiTwinOpt framework makes migrations more efficient. It also helps keep system reliability and service quality good in data centers. The MuFiTwin-Opt framework is designed to handle virtual machine migration. It considers the challenges of cloud resource management. The MuFiTwin-Opt framework provides a solution, for data centers.

publications.title: Quantum-Inspired Hybrid Filtering for Enhanced Noise Reduction in Medical Images
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Intelligent Communication Technologies and Virtual Mobile Networks (ICICV)
publications.abstract: Noise in medical images may obscure small anatomical boundaries, causing distortions in both perception and analysis. This paper proposes a quantum-inspired hybrid denoising approach that (i) identifies the noise pattern via lightweight statistical analysis, (ii) selects classical denoisers suitable for the noise type, and (iii) combines their outputs via a superposition-weighting strategy, followed by a single frequency-domain cleanup operation (wavelet or phase-inspired) and a soft edge recovery step. The proposed framework is designed to remain adaptive across different noise conditions without requiring separate retuning for each image. The proposed approach, as validated through experiments, demonstrates enhanced reconstruction performance for various noise patterns: for Gaussian noise, PSNR is raised from 24.2 dB to 32.7 dB with SSIM = 0.91; for impulse noise, PSNR is raised from 20.1 dB to 31.4 dB with SSIM = 0.89; and for mixed noise, PSNR is raised from 22.3 dB to 29.2 dB with SSIM = 0.86. For the baseline comparison, the proposed approach yields 32.7 dB PSNR, which is superior to the existing Gaussian filter (27.3 dB), median filter (28.0 dB), and bilateral filter (28.6 dB). These results indicate that the proposed method improves reconstruction quality while preserving diagnostically relevant image structure across heterogeneous noise settings.

publications.title: VGG16-based Transfer Learning for Multi-Class Kidney CT Image Classification
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Smart Electronic Devices and Intelligent Systems (ICSEDIS)
publications.abstract: Kidney abnormalities such as cysts, tumors, and kidney stones are commonly evaluated using computed tomography (CT), but manual review of large image volumes is time-consuming and may introduce inter-observer variability. To address this problem, this study presents a transfer-learning framework for multi-class kidney CT image classification using the VGG16 architecture. The model was developed on a publicly available dataset of 12,446 CT slices grouped into four classes: Normal, Cyst, Tumor, and Stone. The workflow combines image resizing, normalization, Gaussian filtering, and controlled training-time augmentation to improve image quality and support model generalization. A stratified 70%/15%/15% split was used for training, validation, and testing. On the held-out test set, the proposed VGG16-based model achieved 92% accuracy, 0.93 macro-precision, 0.91 macro-recall, and 0.92 macro-F1 score, outperforming the shallow CNN and ResNet-50 baselines under the same experimental settings. These findings indicate that transfer learning can provide a practical and computationally efficient solution for automated kidney CT screening and may support radiologists by improving diagnostic consistency and workflow efficiency.

publications.title: Improving Satellite Imagery using Artificial Intelligence
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
publications.abstract: High-Resolution images are required for satellite sensing, and Super Resolution (SR) provides a feasible solution. Super Resolution Image Reconstruction involves generating a High-Resolution (HR) output image from a Low-Resolution (LR) input image. The recent developments in Deep Learning techniques have boosted the capability of image enhancement methods such as Super Resolution, achieving better performance compared to traditional approaches.In this paper, we explore the performance of various training methods used to achieve Super Resolution, while explaining the overall process in simple terms. Additionally, we validate the effectiveness of the generated SR images using a practical implementation of Road Detection through Semantic Segmentation. This provides an added perspective over conventional evaluation metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and the Human Visual System (HVS).Our assessment shows that the down-sampling method used to create LR images during training significantly impacts reconstruction performance. Although traditional metrics correlate well with human perception, the use of a semantic segmentation model offers a more application-driven evaluation method. The experimental results indicate that SR outputs with higher visual clarity contribute to better segmentation accuracy, making this combined framework suitable for real-world satellite image enhancement.

publications.title: An Insightful Approach to Cardiomegaly through CNN and Feature Mapping
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Computational Intelligence for Security, Communication and Sustainable Development (CISCSD)
publications.abstract: The study presents a new approach to identifying cardiomegaly using advanced convolutional neural networks, more specifically, MobileNet and VGG architectures, with interpretative feature maps. Cardiomegaly, or an enlarged heart, is an important sign of particular cardiovascular disorders. Consistently, this topic is an early finding in individual x-ray projection, and because of the general precision of classical methods, innovative deep learning algorithms are needed. In the first stage, the MobileNet and VGG models are designed on distinct heart photo galleries used to cardiac image classification. Systems are seen throughout the domain as vital utilities designed for photo classification. Ultimately, to simplify the solution, an interpreted feature map is employed. Therefore, the technique becomes more reliable, and the design presents a quantitative statement of whether the accessible results say anything concerning the causes of the cardiomegaly estimates. This research has been extensively tested with datasets and produces better results than the existing methods. The presented model grammar map is interpretable, which aids in the medical professional’s comprehension of the model’s prioritizes and boosts their self-assurance in the diagnostic procedure. Furthermore, the novel approach is versatile with various imaging modalities and patient populace, which suggests extensive practical plays. With the help of an interpretable feature map and the combined usage of VGG appearances and MobileNet advantages, this work complements to the field of substantiation the identification of cardiomegaly. As a final point, the introduced model acquires an excellent amount of truthfulness and resolves a serious predicament of interpretability. Thus, it satisfies the growing stress on lucidness and dependability of deep learning applications in medical substantiation.

An Efficient Framework to Detect Intracranial Hemorrhage Using Hybrid Deep Neural Networks
publications.abstract: Intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) is a serious medical condition that necessitates a prompt and exhaustive medical diagnosis. This paper presents a multi-label ICH classification issue with six different types of hemorrhages, namely epidural (EPD), intraparenchymal (ITP), intraventricular (ITV), subarachnoid (SBC), subdural (SBD), and Some. A patient may experience numerous hemorrhages at the same time in some situations. A CT scan of a patient's skull is used to detect and classify the type of ICH hemorrhage(s) present. First, our model determines whether there is a hemorrhage or not; if there is a hemorrhage, the model attempts to identify the type of hemorrhage(s). In this paper, we present a hybrid deep learning approach that combines convolutional neural network (CNN) and Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) approaches (Conv-LSTM). In addition, to propose viable solutions for the problem, we used a Systematic Windowing technique with a Conv-LSTM. To ensure the efficacy of the proposed model, experiments are conducted on the RSNA dataset. The suggested model provides higher sensitivity (93.87%), specificity (96.45%), precision (95.21%), and accuracy (95.14%). In addition, the obtained F1 score results outperform existing deep neural network-based algorithms.

publications.title: A review on Machine Learning based IDS approaches in Wireless sensor networks
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Advanced Computing and Communication Systems (ICACCS)
publications.abstract: In wireless sensor networks (WSNs), sensors are scattered in a particular region to record and evaluate the physical data from the environment. They are widely utilised in various applications, including healthcare, event detection, agriculture, and disaster management. However, the challenges in WSNs include high bandwidth demand, energy consumption, route design, quality of service (QoS) provisioning, unusual activities, etc. However, numerous ways are being considered to solve the aforementioned difficulties. Detecting abnormal network movements is one of the most difficult challenges. An intrusion detection system (IDS) is a productive way to detect infiltration effectively. However, the growth of contemporary technologies necessitates using an effective IDS strategy. As a result, many academicians focus on reducing and eliminating anomalous network security vulnerabilities. According to the findings, machine learning techniques are more critical in addressing these issues. The accuracy of several machine learning algorithms for detecting intrusion in WSNs is investigated in this work. Furthermore, this paper examines the various datasets, performance measurements, and future directions.
keywords: Key distribution in wireless sensor networks

publications.title: An Efficient Framework to Detect Cracks in Rail Tracks Using Neural Network Classifier
publications.abstract: The detection of defects or cracks in rail track plays an important role in railway management, which prevents train accidents in both summer and rainy seasons. During summer, the cracks are formed on the track which slips the train wheel. In rainy environment, the rail tracks are affected by corrosion which also produced cracks on it. Methods: In present method, the cracks or defects are detected Echo image display device or semi conduction magnetism sensor devices which consumes more time. The proposed method enhances the track image using adaptive histogram equalization technique and further features as Grey Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) and Local Binary Pattern (LBP) feature are extracted from the enhanced rail track image. These extracted features are trained and classified using neural network classifier which classifies the rail track image into either cracked or non-cracked image. The novelty of this work is to use soft computing approach for the detection of cracks in rail tracks. This methodology is trained by several crack images which are obtained from different environment. This method automatically classifies the current image based on the trained patterns, thus improves the classification accuracy. Findings: The performance of the proposed system achieves the accuracy rate of 94.9%, with respect to manually crack detected and segmented images.

publications.title: Colon Cancer Classification Using EfficientNetB0 Using Convolutional Block Attention Module
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Emerging Research in Computational Science (ICERCS)
publications.abstract: Timely and accurate detection of colon cancer is essential for enhancing patient outcomes and supporting clinical diagnosis. The study introduces a deep learning-based classification model that combines EfficientB0 with the CBAM to enhance feature extraction from histopathological images. A balanced dataset containing 4000 images for each class was used for reliable training. The preprocessing process includes resizing, normalising, and augmenting through rotation, zooming, shifting, and flipping to improve model robustness and reduce overfitting. EfficientB0 provides strong feature extraction and the integration with the convolution block attention module to focus on the most informative spatial and channel-level features. Experimental results show the model has attained 99.3% accuracy, precision of 100%, 98.6% recall and an AUC score of 1, showing excellent performance in classification. The confusion matrix confirms the model's reliability by indicating zero false positives and a small number of false negatives detected by the model. Overall, the proposed model can be applied to real real-time environment for intrusion detection.

publications.title: Efficient gastric tumor detection from endoscopic images using trans-mapped learning models
Femorotibial degeneration equilibrium analysis for objective and clinically interpretable knee osteoarthritis stratification
publications.abstract: Radiographic evaluation of knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is subject to inter-observer variability and limited objectivity, particularly in early disease stages. This study aimed to develop and validate a clinically interpretable framework for objective KOA identification and severity stratification by quantifying anatomical and functional degenerative imbalance from routine knee radiographs. We propose a novel Femorotibial Degeneration Equilibrium Analysis (FDEA) framework that models KOA as a progressive biomechanical imbalance process rather than an appearance-based classification task. Patient-specific anatomical stability anchors were first extracted to establish a femorotibial reference framework. A virtual mechanical load axis was then projected to quantify medial-lateral load drift, while joint space integrity was assessed using continuity tracing without pixel-wise segmentation. Directional degeneration gradients were further estimated to capture compartment-specific disease progression. These clinically meaningful indicators were integrated using orthopaedic reasoning rules to derive an objective equilibrium loss score for KOA severity stratification. The proposed method was evaluated using knee radiographs from the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) dataset with expert Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grading as the reference standard and was compared with joint space width measurement, texture-based analysis, shape deformation analysis, and radiologist rule-based scoring. External validation was performed on an independent subset from the Multicenter Osteoarthritis Study (MOST). FDEA demonstrated superior agreement with expert KL grading (Cohen's κ = 0.86 ± 0.04; p < 0.01) and achieved higher sensitivity for early-stage KOA (92.4% ± 3.1%) and specificity for advanced disease (94.1% ± 2.8%) than all comparative methods. Assessment time did not differ significantly from conventional radiographic evaluation. The proposed FDEA framework offers a transparent, clinically interpretable decision-support tool that complements conventional grading and supports early diagnosis and treatment planning in knee osteoarthritis.

publications.title: Design and Implementation of a Web-Based Daily Wage Worker Finder System for Efficient Labor Matching
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Control Systems (ICICCS)
publications.abstract: The lack of structure of a digital platform has become a constant problem in urban setting where supply and demand of daily wage skilled workers (plumbers, electricians, carpenters) is not well aligned. The paper is a proposal to create an actual Web-Based Daily Wage Worker Finder System that will facilitate real-time and location-based matching of service seekers and verified workers. The service platform allows registering workers, managing their profiles (dynamics, skills, location) and complex searching and filtering. Trust and quality are guaranteed through a bidirectional rating and an appraisal system. The system is mobile responsive and updated in real time; this makes it more powerful as it empowers the unorganized labor sector by making them more visible, increasing employment opportunities, and making them financially inclusive. The solution can solve the unemployment problem, support inclusive growth, and show a scalable effect by uniting citizens and workers with the help of an effective, open ecosystem of workforce management with modern web technologies.

publications.title: Bio inspired Coati optimization and sparse convolutional encoding framework for intelligent epileptic seizure detection
publications.abstract: Epileptic seizure detection is crucial for clinical diagnosis and ongoing patient monitoring, especially for those with chronic epilepsy. EEG-based seizure detection leverages the brain’s electrical signals to capture temporal and spatial variations that characterize seizure events. However, seizure patterns are often non-linear, patient-specific, and temporally dynamic, making their detection complex and error-prone. Current methods that use machine learning and deep learning models are constrained by challenges such as irrelevant feature inclusion, overfitting, poor generalization, and ineffective management of high-dimensional EEG data. To address these challenges, a novel model is proposed in this research work by incorporating Coati Optimization Algorithm-Based Feature Selection with Convolutional Sparse Autoencoder for accurate and efficient epileptic seizure detection. The proposed model aims to reduce feature redundancy through biologically inspired optimization and improve learning through sparse, high-level feature representations. The methodology was evaluated on the benchmark UCI Epileptic Seizure Recognition Dataset, and experimental analysis ensures the model robust performance with an accuracy of 96.5%, sensitivity of 95.2%, specificity of 97.3%, precision of 96.0%, F1-score of 95.6%, and an AUC of 97.8%. These results of proposed model outperform traditional classifiers such as CNN, SVM with PCA, Random Forest, k-NN, and Deep Autoencoder across all metrics. The integration of optimized feature selection with sparse convolutional encoding contributed significantly to the model’s ability to generalize and minimize false detections, offering a promising tool for automated and reliable seizure detection in clinical and real-time environments.

publications.title: An Interactive Application for Eggplant Quality Detection Using YOLOV8-E
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Inventive Research in Computing Applications (ICIRCA)
publications.abstract: Global food security depends on agriculture, and produce has to be of good quality if it is to be successful on the market. Efficient quality assessment of eggplants is important as they are widely cultivated for their nutritional value and hence have to meet industry standards. Manually inspecting eggplant quality is a traditional method but is time consuming, inconsistent and labor intensive. In this paper, an interactive application for detecting eggplant quality using YOLOv8-E, a sophisticated deep learning model that is optimized for real-time object detection is introduced. With the proposed system, users can upload their eggplant images or use a live camera feed to scan eggplant, and the model can quickly judge the quality of factors such as size, shape, color consistency, and the presence of visible defects. This android application takes images, processes them efficiently and immediately gives back feedback by marking detected issues and classifying eggplants into different grade. This system was designed to be lightweight, scalable and user friendly and is well suited to deployment in agricultural fields, supply chain management or retail environments. The application integrates deep learning into the quality assessment process and improves decision making, reduces labor cost, minimize post harvest loss, and guarantees that only high quality eggplants reach consumers. Using this new approach helps to modernize the way agricultural practices are done by automating quality control as well as optimizing the distribution of fresh produce.

publications.title: Enhanced leukemia prediction using hybrid ant colony and ant lion optimization for gene selection and classification
publications.abstract: Gene selection plays a crucial role in the pre-processing of microarray data, aiming to identify a small set of genes that enhances classification accuracy and reduces costs. Traditional methods, such as Genetic Algorithms (GA) and Maximum Relevance Minimum Redundancy (MRMR), have been widely used, but bio-inspired algorithms like Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) and Ant Lion Optimizer (ALO) have shown promising results. These algorithms are based on natural processes: ACO mimics the foraging behavior of ants, while ALO models the hunting strategy of ant-lion larvae. However, both approaches face challenges like premature convergence and inefficient feature space mapping when used individually. To address these issues, this work introduces a hybrid ACO-ALO method, combining the strengths of both algorithms. The proposed hybrid approach enhances feature selection by improving accuracy, reducing computational complexity, and boosting classifier performance. The proposed model, which identifies the optimal feature set for classification using Support Vector Machine (SVM), has achieved an impressive prediction accuracy of 93.94 %. Results on microarray datasets for leukemia prediction show that the hybrid approach outperforms other methods in terms of both effectiveness and efficiency. This work demonstrates the potential of hybrid optimization techniques in bioinformatics for better gene selection and cancer diagnosis.•Hybrid ACO-ALO approach combines strengths of both algorithms for better feature selection.•Enhances classifier performance while reducing computational complexity.•Outperforms traditional methods on leukemia prediction datasets.

publications.title: Epileptic Seizure Prediction through ML And DL Models: A Survey
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
publications.abstract: Epileptic seizures are unpredictable and pose significant risks to individuals affected by epilepsy. Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals offer a promising avenue for early seizure prediction, enabling timely intervention and improved quality of life for patients. This survey paper provides a comprehensive review of Deep learning (DL) and Machine learning (ML) learning techniques applied to EEG-based epileptic seizure prediction. It covers traditional ML models, advanced DL architectures, and optimization algorithms, highlighting their effectiveness and limitations. Additionally, the paper discusses feature extraction methods, signal processing techniques, and evaluation metrics used in this domain. Real-world applications, current challenges, and future research directions are explored to offer a holistic view of the field. By examining state-of-the-art methods, this survey aims to provide valuable insights into the development of robust, real-time seizure prediction systems, fostering advancements in clinical applications and patient care.

publications.title: Ensemble Techniques for the Prediction of Heart Disease with Reduced Entropy
authors: A. M. J. Md. Zubair Rahman
publications.journalOrConferenceName: IEEE International Conference on Interdisciplinary Approaches in Technology and Management for Social Innovation (IATMSI)
publications.abstract: Healthcare industry generates a vast amount of data, the majority of which is sophisticated and massive in size. This information, however, is not "extracted" in order to uncover hidden facts for effective decision-making. Diagnosing heart disease, a noncommunicable disease, is one of the more difficult problems in medicine because it entails the patient's past health history. An accurate and effective automated system can be quite beneficial in detecting cardiac problems. Modern data mining techniques may be able to solve this issue. In the healthcare industry, various information-extracting technologies such as association rule mining, classification, and clustering are used to forecast cardiac disease. In order to address this issue, the research investigates the use of machine learning methods for cardiac disease prediction, including Naive Bayes (NB), logarithmic regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), the Decision Tree (DT), Random Forests (RF), and the k-nearest-neighbor algorithm (KNN). The Random Forest ensemble technique outperforms with 99% accuracy.

Vigilant Salp Swarm Algorithm for Feature Selection
publications.abstract: Feature selection (FS) averts the consideration of unwanted features which may tend the classification algorithm to classify wrongly. Choosing an optimal feature subset from the given set of features is challenging due to the complex associations present within the features. In non-convex conditions, the gradient-based algorithms suffer due to local optima or saddle points with respect to initial conditions where swarm intelligence algorithms pose a higher chance to converge over the global optima. The Salp Swarm Algorithm (SSA) proposed by Mirjalili et al. is based on the chaining behaviour of sea salps but the algorithm lacks diversity in the exploration stage. Rectifying the exploratory behaviour and testing the algorithm against the FS problem is the motivation behind this work. Three variants of the algorithm are proposed, of which the Vigilant Salp Swarm Algorithm (VSSA) inherits the vigilant mechanism in Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), the second variant and the third variant replace a simple crossover operator and shuffle crossover operator instead of the follower's position update mechanism used in the VSSA to form Vanilla Crossover VSSA (VCVSSA) and Shuffle Crossover VSSA (SCVSSA).

publications.title: Real-Time Sign Language Translator using Vision Transformer for Gesture-to-Speech Conversion
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Smart Systems (ICSCSS)
publications.abstract: The proposed paper is a real-time translation system of sign language which aims at closing the communication gap that exists between deaf or speech-impaired individuals and non-signers. The proposed solution is based on a Vision Transformer (ViT)-based model and supervised learning that can effectively identify hand gestures. In contrast to the conventional approaches that are based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), the system learns the global spatial patterns between landmarks of hands through attention mechanisms. The system receives live video input and processes it with the help of MediaPipe to extract 21 hand landmark points, turning them into feature vectors and classifies these with the ViT model. Gestures which have been identified are translated into text and then into speech with a Text-to-Speech (TTS) engine, allowing real-time communication. High accuracy, low latency and robustness have been shown in experimental results in various environments.

publications.title: A Hybrid Lightweight Framework for Real-Time CCTV-based Accident Detection with Automated Emergency Alert Generation
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Smart Systems (ICSCSS)
publications.abstract: The high rate of growth in road traffic has been a major cause of drastic increase in the number of accidents which have resulted in high demand of effective real-time monitoring and response systems. This paper introduces a hybrid system of accident detection and classification of severity based on CCTV video streams implemented on deep learning. The suggested system is a combination of the YOLOv8s object detector model and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) using MobileNetV3 to guarantee the efficient performance of the system. YOLOv8s is used to identify regions of accidents in the continuous video frames and the CNN model is used to categorize the identified accidents into moderate and severe. The system is trained on a publicly available dataset of more than 15,000 annotated images, which were recorded in a variety of environmental conditions, which guarantees a robust system and generalization. Experimental findings indicate that it has a high detection accuracy with good precision, recall and mAP values and stable classification accuracy. Also, an automated alert system is included to inform emergency services in case of severe accidents identified so that they can respond quicker and have a lesser effect. The suggested framework is minimal and scalable and appropriate to be implemented in intelligent transportation systems and smart city applications.

publications.title: OptiM-RoViT: A Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis Framework with Dynamic Fusion and Noise-Aware Vision Transformers
publications.journalOrConferenceName: Journal of Computational and Cognitive Engineering
publications.abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis has been studied by many researchers because of its capability to understand human emotions through textual and visual data. Despite that, current approaches suffer from feature misalignment, modality imbalance, and a lack of robustness against noisy inputs. A new framework called OptiM-RoViT is proposed, which is built on RoBERTa for processing text and Vision Transformer (ViT) for analyzing images and enhances the model with dynamic modality weighting and Gaussian noise injection techniques. To achieve the best performance, the model uses Optuna-based hyperparameter optimization and can achieve 98.89% accuracy, 0.96 F1-score, and 0.04 false negative rate on the dataset of 10,000 product reviews. Complementary ablation studies also quantify the improvement of each component by enabling significant improvements over baseline architectures. Evaluations against stronger backbones (DeBERTa, Swin-V2) confirm that the proposed fusion mechanism is the primary driver of robustness, outperforming generic state-of-the-art baselines on noisy inputs. The critical challenges in multimodal fusion, including computational scalability and general efficacy, are addressed by the proposed approach, which is also well suited for the real-world applications such as e-commerce and social media analytics. Such adaptation may be explored in other domains as future work, and other modalities can be used to achieve similarly broad applicability. publications.title: Secure Data Transmission in IoT Networks Using Blockchain and Lightweight Cryptography: Safeguarding the Connected Future
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Communication, Security and Artificial Intelligence (ICCSAI)
publications.abstract: The number of connected devices that are part of the IoT has grown at a very fast pace and offered myriad advantages, but also created several problems in the spheres of data security and privacy. As more and more smart devices are being connected to each other, it has become imperative to provide a safe and reliable channel to communicate is essential to ward off ‘jammers' and hackers. This work aims to establish whether the combination of blockchain technology implementation and lightweight cryptographic algorithms can be used to improve security in IoT networks. One more benefit originates from the very nature of the block chain where every record is coded in blocks, this makes it possible to track records due to the decentralized nature of their database thus providing an efficient means of tracking data integrity and when it is being tempered with. Hence, it is easy to implement the proposed lightweight cryptographic algorithm so the IoT device will not have a problem in transmitting secure data as it possesses limited processing and energy capacity. Through the available literature, several methods of lightweight encryption including symmetric encryption and hash functions appropriate for IoT applications to ensure confidentiality and authentication are discussed. Besides, the paper considers how the implementation of smart contracts in blockchain enables providing security policies for automation that react to threats on time, preventing cyber attacks. These technologies in unison provide a strong defense mechanism against these issues which will make IoT more protected and secure for use. The scalability, efficiency and feasibility of the proposed solution has also been presented in this paper and thus the effectiveness of the presented solution has been explored to served as potential real world IoT systems.

publications.title: Exploring Zero-Shot Learning in Natural Language Processing for Cross-Domain Applications
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
publications.abstract: The research assesses how three and two state-of-the-art pre-trained language models (PLMs) function alongside BERT and BioBERT while operating on various natural language processing (NLP) functions which incorporate sentiment analysis, text classification, entity recognition and cross-domain sentiment classification. BERT and BioBERT achieve superior performance than all other models by delivering optimal accuracy ratings together with high precision and recall while obtaining the highest F1-score across all tasks. The generalization ability of BERT enables it to maintain top performance across four different domains which include product reviews, movie reviews, social media content and news articles. BioBERT demonstrates particular effectiveness when handling biomedical Natural Language Processing applications. The model performance of T5 matches BERT although BERT demonstrates better outcomes in specific tasks. RoBERTa together with GPT-2 achieves moderate success in particular use cases but consistently performs below the current best NLP models. BERT-based models demonstrate superior performance in various NLP applications which demonstrates their strength in dealing with complicated operations yet researchers need to investigate RoBERTa and GPT-2 specifically within individual domains to achieve superior outcomes.

publications.title: A Lightweight Multimodal Framework With Dilated CNN Audio Modeling and SE-Enhanced MobileNetV2 for Real-Time Sentiment Analysis of Customer Product Reviews
publications.abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has transformed customer feedback into a multimodal medium, encompassing not only text but also speech, images, and video reviews. Traditional unimodal sentiment analysis approaches—predominantly text-based—fail to capture the rich emotional cues embedded in voice tone, facial expressions, and visual context, often resulting in misclassification in cases of irony or ambiguous expressions. Recent multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) studies have explored fusion strategies across text, audio, and video, but most existing methods either rely on computationally heavy architectures or prioritize text while underutilizing non-textual modalities. This study introduces AViSE-Net (Audio–Video Squeeze-Excitation Network), a lightweight yet discriminative multimodal framework that leverages dilated CNNs for audio and an SE-enhanced MobileNetV2 backbone for video and image data. Key innovations include (i) dilated convolutions in the audio branch for efficient long-range temporal modelling, (ii) channel-wise recalibration through Squeeze-and-Excitation blocks in the video pathway, (iii) fusion with LayerNorm and GELU activations for stable cross-modal integration, and (iv) a progressive unfreezing strategy to accelerate convergence while preserving pretrained visual features. Evaluated on a curated multimodal dataset of customer product reviews, AViSE-Net achieves 97.9% accuracy with ~50% fewer parameters than heavy baseline models such as BiLSTM+ResNet18, while maintaining real-time inference speeds of ~42 fps on GPU. Comparative experiments and ablation studies confirm that each architectural enhancement contributes significantly to the superior performance. These results establish AViSE-Net as a compact, scalable, and deployment-ready solution for real-world multimodal sentiment analysis in e-commerce and consumer feedback applications.

publications.title: An Innovative Method of Developing BI-LSTM and KNN Algorithms for Disintegrating Sentiments Through Reviews
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Advance Computing and Innovative Technologies in Engineering (ICACITE)
publications.abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, schools globally transitioned to online education due to lockdowns, prompting concerns about its acceptance and effectiveness among stakeholders. This study analyzes public sentiment towards e-learning using a dataset of 17,155 tweets collected from social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter. Machine learning and deep learning techniques are employed for text analysis, including sentiment analysis using Senti Word Net, Text Blob, and VADER. Various machine learning models, supported by feature extraction methods like Bag of Words (BoW) and TF-IDF, are used to categorize sentiment with measures such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. Long short term memory (LSTM), k nearest neighbour (KNN) machine classifiers, when combined with BoW data, achieve the highest accuracy. Subject modeling reveals common e-learning challenges, including insufficient network infrastructure, children’s difficulties with online learning, and uncertainties about campus reopening.

publications.title: Enhanced Visuals through Software-Optimized Memory Pipeline
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Computer, Communication and Control
publications.abstract: Image processing algorithms, which supply the image quality, are used by modern mobile devices to capture images. These methods need more RAM to process an image and fix these problems. Software pipelines are utilized to reduce memory usage as much as feasible while maintaining the highest level of flexibility and affordability. Our method uses a line-based buffer software pipeline, which improves image quality and runs at a minimal cost. By transferring only the output to the next phase, the algorithm operates on an individual basis. Each step is completed in less time. Using picture enhancement and noise reduction techniques results in increased productivity, reduced memory consumption, and greater image quality. The applied framework demonstrates noise reduction with the PSNR algorithm and yields good results.

publications.title: Enhancing the Prediction of Underwater Wireless Communication using Machine Learning Techniques and Related Issues
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
publications.abstract: This research aims to enhance the prediction of underwater wireless communication for underwater wireless sensor networks using Logistic Regression compared with Linear Regression Algorithms. To forecast the functionality of underwater wireless sensor networks Linear Regression and Novel Logistic Regression algorithms were used with different training and testing splits with Underwater Acoustic Wireless Sensor. A sample size of 20 (Each 10 from Group 1 and Group 2) is calculated by fixing a G-power of 0.8, alpha and beta values of 0.05 and 0.2, and a confidence interval of 95%. With a statistical significance value of 0.001 (p<0.05), Novel Logistic Regression (87.77% & 12.22%) outperforms Linear Regression (80.17% & 19.32%) in terms of accuracy and Loss which is statistically significant. The Underwater Wireless Communication efficiency were compared with the obtained results for Linear Regression, Logistic Regression proves to have higher accuracy.

publications.title: Classification of Music Genre Audio Signals Using Deep Neural Networks
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Advances in Electrical, Electronics and Computational Intelligence (ICAEECI)
publications.abstract: Music is one of the fundamental parts in our lives. Music gives us amusement and relax when we feel empty. Everyone in the society will generally listen music of specific genre subject to how they are feeling right now. It turns into an exceptionally feverish and complex undertaking to classify the music manually. Thus, there is a requirement for a model to classify the music into various Genres which can be utilized in some genuine applications. In this task, a deep learning model is proposed to arrange the music into various types. The proposed model depends on the Convolutional Neural Networks, Which are generally excellent at image pattern recognition. The model is prepared over GZTAN dataset which contains ten classes with hundred music records connected with every sort. The music documents are first changed over into Mel-spectrograms utilizing librosa and afterward those spectrograms are fed as input to the developed Convolutional Neural Network model for preparing. So that the network extracts some features based on audio genre frequency and learns about different genres that are helpful to classify the unknown music file into respective genre.

publications.title: The Current State of Software Engineering Employing Methods Derived from Artificial Intelligence and Outstanding Challenges
publications.journalOrConferenceName: IEEE International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
publications.abstract: Although AI has become a buzzword for self-organizing IT applications; its significance to software engineering has not been rigorously examined. To evaluate the current state of advancement, the potential for future development and the risks of AI application to software engineering, this study combines a systematic review of previous research in the field with five qualitative interviews with software developers who use or want to use AI tools in their daily work routines. Research organises findings about the software improvement life sequence. Results show that AI's greatest achievements and potential lie in three areas: a) the systematic evaluation of these data in neural networks; b) the structured analysis of big data pools to discover patterns and novel information clusters; and c) the automated automation of lengthy routine jobs in software development and testing using algorithms, such as for debugging and documentation. As a result, AI shortens the development cycle, reduces expenses, and increases productivity. AI has thus far been dependent on human-made structures and has primarily been reproductive; nonetheless, the automation of software engineering jobs has a major advantage: the creative capacity of human developers is multiplied when using AI tools effectively.

publications.abstract: The beginning of this chapter briefly presents a few examples of scams and hacks that we have all experienced. The AT&T example is taken from a letter the author received explaining that some personal data was illegally obtained and how along with a few recommendations about how customers whose data was put at risk by poor cybersecurity on the part of a major communications provider should proceed to protect themselves. This example seems to suggest that senior executives of this organization are minimally engaged in cybersecurity. In the future and starting at the Board of Director's level, all levels of management including those in the C suite must change. Moreover, according to the CIA, data security has three core principles: Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability. These three core principles will need new and enhanced skills to ensure the organization address data security as a High Reliability Organization operating at a very high level of performance. Finally, as with all risk and governance efforts, cybersecurity risk mitigation must be aligned and integrated with the Enterprise Risk Management governance, policies, and procedures.

publications.title: Histopathological image analysis and enhanced diagnostic accuracy explainability for oral cancer detection
publications.abstract: Deep learning (DL) has transformed medical imaging, particularly in the realm of oral cancer (OC) diagnosis using histopathological images. Timely detection of OC is es-sential for enhancing precision medicine and saving lives. However, incorrect diagnosis may impede effective treatment. In this study, we have proposed a DL model for OC classification, enhanced diagnosis decision-making and interpretability. We achieve this by starting with colour normalisation of histopathology images using the Vaha-dane 3-stain parameter normalisation and watershed segmentation method, followed by tiling and augmentation. Key features are selected using the weighted Fisher score (WFS) to address class imbalance. The U-Net classifier has been improved by using feature-based inputs instead of full images, reducing computational complexity and training time. The integration of Vahadane normalisation for consistent preprocessing across samples, WFS, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) addresses critical challenges in histopathological image analysis. The proposed model surpasses exist-ing approaches with a classification accuracy of 99.54%, and it outperforms Dense- Net201 and VGG10 in precision and reliability. The efficiency in handling imbal-anced datasets and explainability features make it suitable for early precise OC detec-tion, which can reduce diagnostic errors and enhance treatment outcomes.

publications.abstract: Stable communication and quality Wi-Fi systems, in particular, are among the main challenges posed by the variable nature of wireless communication environments.The ability to predict Wi-Fi link quality is of prime importance in making the network perform excellently, making the connectivity reliable, and preventing service disruptions.This paper reports on the potential of machine learning models to predict Wi-Fi link quality with high precision, while focusing on low-complexity models that can be deployed in resource-limited hardware environments.The assessment features several machine learning algorithms such as Random Forest, Stacking Classifier, Voting Classifier, and Decision Tree that use a linear combination of exponential moving averages to make predictions.The models are trained on a dataset created from real Wi-Fi link data, where the output is classified as one of three link quality levels: Very Good, Good, and Poor.The findings prove that the models are able to deliver predictions that are highly accurate, efficient, and even scalable in scenarios where the computational power is very limited.

publications.title: Modified Imperialist Competitive Algorithm (MICA) For Smart Heart Disease Prediction in IoT System
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Distributed Computing and Electrical Circuits and Electronics (ICDCECE)
publications.abstract: For the detection and prognosis of heart disease, Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) technology has recently been implemented in healthcare systems. The intended study's main objective is to foresee heart illness using medical data and imaging to classify data. Preprocessing is done on the input dataset to deal with missing values and incorrect data. IoT devices analyse the data they receive from patients, physicians, or nurses using the Modified Imperialist Competitive Algorithm (MICA). The IoT device's analysis of the data allows for effective and informed judgements to be made by humans, robots, and even other IoT devices. A modified imperialist competitive algorithm is suggested in this research in order to pinpoint the essential characteristics of heart disease. The Modified Imperialist Competitive Algorithm is used to select features for the diagnosis of heart disease (MICA). The improved self-adaptive Bayesian algorithm (ISABA) technique is then used to classify the chosen features into normal and abnormal states. For detecting normal sensor data and abnormal sensor data, respectively, the ISABA approach achieved accuracy of 96.85% and 98.31%. publications.title: Base-Station Slot Antenna for Milli-Meter Wave Application Using SIW Technology
publications.journalOrConferenceName: 2025 10th International Conference on Smart Structures and Systems (ICSSS)
publications.abstract: This work analyzes a slot-based antenna structure designed to operate at millimetre-wave frequencies. The investigation focuses on a rectangular slot etched on the top conductor of the SIW and includes design, modelling, and performance evaluation. Copper is the conducting material, while Roggers is the material utilised to construct SIW structures. Parameters like S11, voltage standing wave ratio, and Radiation Pattern (RP) are used to assess the suggested model. High isolation and efficient impedance matching at the ports are revealed by S parameter simulations. With values ranging from roughly 1.2 to 3.5, the VSWR analysis shows moderate to good impedance matching. The simulated field patterns match the performance parameters of the device, and high field intensity is seen close to the SIW’s edges and perforations. At certain frequencies, the device shows very little reflection, indicating improved transmission efficiency. This showed that the millimetre wave frequency is a good fit for the suggested design.

publications.title: Early Parkinson’s disease diagnosis for analyzing handwritten spiral and wave images using deep learning models
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Journal of Nutrition, Pharmacology, Neurological Diseases
publications.abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a chronic neurological condition affecting millions globally, resulting from the deterioration or damage of dopamine-producing brain cells, crucial for motor function regulation. PD manifests with symptoms like impaired movement, balance issues, and posture problems. In order to decrease its progression and improve patients’ quality of life, early identification is essential. This study combines deep transfer learning with a Stochastic Gradient scheduler to present a unique method for handwriting analysis-based PD prediction. The study utilizes the NIATS datasets, comprising handwriting samples from individuals both with and without PD. Six distinct deep learning models—VGG16, VGG19, ResNet18, ResNet50, ResNet101, and ViT—are evaluated to determine their efficacy in PD prediction. Performance comparison across these models focuses on three key metrics: accuracy, precision, and F1 score. The results show that the VGG19 model has the highest average accuracy of 97.27% when using the suggested methods. This result highlights how well the Stochastic Gradient Learning Method works with deep transfer learning to improve the accuracy of PD predictions using handwriting data. This work offers important new information about how to use cutting-edge machine learning methods for PD early diagnosis and treatment, which could lead to better patient outcomes and more successful clinical interventions. This study uses hand-drawn spiral and wave patterns to investigate different deep transfer learning models for early PD detection. To reduce model overfitting, cutting-edge data augmentation methods like Aug Mix and Pix mix were used. With an accuracy of 97.27%, VGG19 outperformed the other models in the evaluation.
