publications.title: Enhancing Lung Segmentation Through Preprocessing of Medical Data Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publications.journalOrConferenceName: IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics, Cognition and Machine Learning Applications (ICCCMLA)
publications.abstract: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death for women and the second leading cause of cancer-related death for men, according to a report by the World Health Organization in 2020. Detecting lung cancer through a three-dimensional X-ray of a patient's lungs, or a chest X-ray, is a common practice, but it can lead to errors caused by the human factor. To address this issue, advanced algorithms, and CAD technologies can be used to detect lung cancer. A network model can be trained using deep structural learning to detect details and deviations in the X-ray image. However, creating an accurate model using this technique is both time-consuming and advanced, and the model must be trained correctly. Despite the extensive research on various network architectures, the preprocessing technique of lung segmentation and its influence on such models remains largely unexplored. Thus, in this study, we aim to investigate the effect of applying lung segmentation to the training and testing data used by the CNN model on accuracy and loss. To achieve this, we developed two CNN models, one with and one without lung segmentation, respectively. The models were evaluated and compared, and our results demonstrate that lung segmentation can mitigate overtraining, resulting in a significant improvement in accuracy. We anticipate that this study will pave the way for further research in similar problem areas.

publications.title: Machine Learning Models for Classification of Sensitive Financial Documents
publications.journalOrConferenceName: IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics, Cognition and Machine Learning Applications (ICCCMLA)
publications.abstract: This research proposes a machine learning-based approach for the automated classification of sensitive financial documents. The proposed method utilizes Support Vector Machines (SVM), Naive Bayes, and a rule-based classifier to classify categorized financial documents accurately. The system extracts relevant features from the documents and trains the models to classify them into predefined categories. The performance of each model is evaluated, and the results are compared to identify the best-performing model. The result shows that all methods achieved satisfactory results in terms of accuracy, F-Score, and execution time. The experimental results show that the Naïve Bayes classifier outperforms the other models, achieving an accuracy of 95% in classifying the financial documents. The total time consumption, which takes into account manual handling of missorts and classification of files that could not be sorted, was significantly lower for the Naive Bayes implementations. The proposed method can significantly reduce the time and effort required for manual classification and can improve the accuracy of the classification process. The version with a tolerance level performed best and showed higher precision, but lower accuracy. This research can have significant implications in the financial industry, where the automated classification of sensitive financial documents can improve operational efficiency and reduce the risk of errors.

publications.title: AI-Based Crop Demand Forecasting and Cultivation Optimization for Market Price Stabilization in Smart Agriculture
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Communication, Computing and Emerging Technologies (IC3ET)
publications.abstract: India's agricultural economy continues to face persistent challenges in stabilizing crop prices, balancing production with demand, and securing farmer profitability. Despite progress in precision farming and digital marketplaces, cultivation decisions remain largely reactive, leading to oversupply or shortage cycles. This paper proposes DynaCropNet, an AI-based Crop Demand Forecasting and Cultivation Optimization Framework that integrates multi-source datasets from eNAM and Data.gov.in to forecast demand, predict market prices, and recommend region-specific crop allocations. The model employs Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), ARIMA, and Prophet components enhanced by a Temporal–Spatial Fusion Transformer and a Differentiable Optimization Layer for end-to-end learning. A reinforcement module dynamically adjusts cultivation strategies based on simulated market feedback. Experimental results show that DynaCropNet achieves RMSE$=27.85$, MAPE$=6.92 \%$, and reduces price variance by 57.9%, while improving farmer income by 16.5% across major states. The system effectively synchronizes cultivation planning with forecasted demand, ensuring price stability and equitable economic outcomes. This research demonstrates how integrating AI-driven forecasting with optimization and reinforcement learning can transform agriculture from reactive management to predictive and prescriptive intelligence for national food security and market resilience.

publications.title: Deep Vision Transformer with Tasmanian Devil Optimization for Multiclass Paddy Disease Detection and Classification for Precision Agriculture
publications.journalOrConferenceName: Journal of Electronics Electromedical Engineering and Medical Informatics
publications.abstract: Rice is the daily consumed crop all over the country and other parts of the world. Rice is cultivated in most of the states. Nevertheless, rice plant diseases deteriorate the quantity and quality of the crop. Rice plants are affected by various conditions, for example: sheath blight, foot rot, and so on, producing a loss in the farming yield. Therefore, earlier disease recognition in crops is important. Performing intelligent Farming is a hot zone of investigation to prevent more harm to crops. The extensive growth of Deep Learning (DL) makes it probable to attain the objective of disease recognition in crops. In this manuscript, we introduce a new Deep Vision Transformer with Tasmanian Devil Optimization for Multiclass Paddy Disease Detection and Classification (DViTTDO-MPDDC) technique for Precision Agriculture. The major intention of the DViTTDO-MPDDC technique focuses on the automatic classification and recognition of paddy plant diseases. To accomplish this, the DViTTDO-MPDDC technique uses the wiener filter (WF) technique for the noise removal process. Besides, the vision transformer (ViT) technique is used for feature extraction purposes. Additionally, the attention mechanism-based convolutional neural network with bidirectional long short-term memory (AM-CNN-BiLSTM) technique is used for the paddy disease detection process. Eventually, the TDO algorithm is exploited for the hyperparameter fine-tuning of the AM-CNN-BiLSTM model. To demonstrate the good classification outcome of the DViTTDO-MPDDC algorithm, a wide variety of models occurs on the benchmark database. The extensive comparable findings ensured the betterment of the DViTTDO-MPDDC method over the current methods.

publications.title: ENHANCING CONTEXT-AWARE DIALOGUE SYSTEMS VIA MULTI-MODAL FUSION AND HIERARCHICAL SELF-ATTENTION
authors: Dr CHINTAKINDI SRINIVAS , VIJAYAGANTH R , Dr B.RANGA SWAMY , Dr SRAVANI KOPPURAVURI , Dr HARI JYOTHULA , Dr SUBBA RAO POLAMURI, Dr N. NEELIMA , KADIYALA SUDHAKAR
publications.journalOrConferenceName: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
publications.abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to context-aware dialogue systems through the integration of multi-modal fusion architecture and hierarchical self-attention mechanisms. The proposed model, Multi-Modal Hierarchical Attention Network (MMHAN), addresses critical challenges in modern conversational AI by effectively incorporating visual, textual, and historical context cues to generate more coherent and contextually appropriate responses. Unlike prior works that treat modalities independently or apply flat attention across dialogue history, MMHAN introduces a three-level hierarchical attention mechanism combined with a cross-modal fusion component. Experiments on three benchmark datasets (MultiWOZ 2.1, Ubuntu Dialogue Corpus, and Visual Dialog) demonstrate that MMHAN outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by 7.2% on response relevance and 9.1% on context retention. Human evaluation shows MMHAN responses were preferred in 76.3% of comparisons. A novel metric, Cross-Modal Coherence Score (CMCS), correlates strongly with human judgments (r=0.82). With only 15% additional parameters over text-only models, MMHAN is efficient and suitable for real-world deployment.

publications.title: Revolutionizing IoT Network Security with Deep Learning-Anomaly Detection Model
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Electronics and Sustainable Communication Systems (ICESC)
publications.abstract: The term “Internet of Things” (IoT) is used to describe the collection of data and the connectivity of items to the web that requires little to no human interaction. The IoT is a network of interconnected devices that can collect and disseminate information. Increased security and privacy worries accompany the launch of new devices due to the proliferation of Internet connections and the development of cutting-edge technology like the IoT. These days, the IoT is used everywhere, but especially in logistics, manufacturing, and healthcare. While these emerging IoT applications greatly enhance the usefulness of smart objects, they also present new security risks. Because of this, adapting existing intrusion detection systems (IDS) for use with IoT networks is a topic of intense study. Many IDS experts have found success with machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques. By combining deep extraction through the Convolutional autoencoder with deep learning to identify the best features, this work delivers an improved IDS that can be used for anomaly detection. Improves to the deep learning approach include an evaluation of hyperparameter effectiveness, a stage of feature pruning using an autoencoder neural network, and an examination of the sturdiness of the most effective deep neural networks for circumstances exaggerated by Gaussian noise over some of the features in question. Despite the noise, the results show that the formed IoT dataset is useful for anomaly detection with deep learning methods.

publications.title: Convolutional Neural Network-based Covid-19 Analysis with Internet of Things
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Advanced Technologies in Intelligent Control, Environment, Computing & Communication Engineering (ICATIECE)
publications.abstract: The very hazardous respiratory illness known as COVID-2 (SARS-CoV-2), which is the root cause of the even more serious illness known as COVID-19, was caused by the COVID-2 virus. The COVID-19 virus was identified in Wuhan City, China, in the month of December in 2019. It began in China and then spread to other parts of the world before it was officially classified as a pandemic. It has had a significant impact on day-to-day life, the welfare of people in general, and the economy of the whole globe. It is of the utmost importance, particularly in the beginning stages of treatment, to pinpoint the constructive experiences that are useful at the proper time. The identification of this virus involves a substantial number of tests, each of which takes a certain amount of time; nevertheless, there are currently no other automated tool kits that can be used in their place. X-ray photos of the chest that are obtained via the use of radiology imaging methods may provide significant insight into the COVID-19 infection if they are analysed carefully. An accurate diagnosis of the infection may be obtained via the application of deep learning techniques, which are applied to radiological images and make use of cutting-edge technology such as artificial intelligence. Patients who reside in distant places, where it may not be feasible for them to have rapid access to medical facilities, may benefit from this kind of analysis throughout the course of their therapy. One of the deep learning strategies that are used in the creation of the model that has been proposed is the use of convolutional neural networks. The images of chest X-rays are analysed by these networks to detect whether a person has a positive or negative result for the Covid gene.

publications.abstract: Keeping data safe and sound in cloud systems is important. So, new ways need to be found so private information can't get changed or seen without permission by wrong people. This research gives a new blockchain method to make data reliability better in cloud systems. We show how our suggested method is better and more useful than others in keeping data safe. We do this by doing a deep study and comparing with other ways that are currently used. When we look at how many transactions a system can handle, the time it takes for things to happen and its ability to grow bigger without problems, our suggested method does better than other solutions in Comparing Performance. It handles 1000 transactions each second, with a time delay of only 10 milliseconds. It can work well for up to one hundred nodes on the network while still showing it's efficient and able to keep growing bigger over time. The Data Comparison shows that our suggested way is very good at finding out false information, and it can find 98% of this. Besides, it quickly recovers data with a downtime of only 2 hours. This makes it different from old ways by making sure data can't be changed and there are strong checks on who did what. Security Check shows our new plan works well. It stops people spending money twice, stands up against cheating tactics and keeps a strong Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) at 99.9%. The Proof of Stake agreement is both easy on energy and safe. publications.abstract: In this ambitious agricultural project, cutting-edge technologies such as Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) are harnessed to revolutionize farming practices in India. The primary focus lies in automating vital tasks like crop disease detection, crop recommendation, and fertilizer suggestion, which are traditionally laborious and time-consuming for farmers. Leveraging recent advancements in ML algorithms, a comprehensive solution is envisaged. This innovative approach involves the integration of sophisticated models into a user-friendly website, creating a seamless user experience. Through this platform, farmers gain access to automated tools that significantly enhance their crop management strategies. The platform provides a comprehensive solution by combining deep learning-based crop disease detection mechanisms, intelligent crop recommendation systems, and effective fertilizer recommendations derived from machine learning algorithms. This combination of technologies helps farmers maximize their overall crop yields and minimize losses caused by diseases in addition to streamlining farming procedures. The synergy of ML, and DL on a unified web interface stands as a testament to the transformative power of technology in agriculture, marking a pivotal step toward sustainable and efficient farming practices in India.

publications.abstract: This literature review examines evolving trends in audio-to-text and text summarization techniques applied to YouTube video content. With the rapid expansion of online video platforms, the demand for efficient transcription and summarization of multimedia data has grown significantly. This study offers a comprehensive analysis of current methodologies, algorithms, and tools for converting audio content to text, highlighting the intricacies of speech recognition technologies and their applicability in various contexts. Additionally, the survey explores text summarization techniques specifically designed for YouTube videos, including both extractive and abstractive methods. It assesses their effectiveness in condensing lengthy video transcripts into concise and coherent textual representations. Special emphasis is given to NLP (Natural Language Processing) algorithms and ML (Machine Learning) models that aid in extracting essential information while maintaining contextual relevance.
affiliation: KPR Institute of Engineering and Technology

publications.title: Cascade face classification framework based mask detection of real time images using deep learning approach
publications.abstract: Detecting the faces with mask in efficient way is becoming incredibly valuable, as it can be used in COVID-19 situation as well as it can play a major role to follow and identify criminals or terrorists. Because of the high occlusions that result in the loss of face information, masked face identification is a far more difficult process. The proposed scheme employed a way to states that a person had worn a mass or not. A simple convolutional neural network (CNN) model is developed using deep learning and combining Tensor Flow, Keras, Scikit-learn, and Open-CV to make the system as accurate as possible. Moreover, using the Flask framework and a webcam, a real-time detection application has been created that is capable of accurately predicting a person has wear a mask and not, as well as showing a label in the right corner of the image. Categorical cross-entropy is applied as a loss function. The proposed model’s validation accuracy is 97.45 percent. Anyone on the live stream who is not wearing a mask has a rectangle around their face that is red, with the dialogue "NO MASK," while anyone who is wearing a mask gets a rectangle around their face that is green.
affiliation: KPR Institute of Engineering and Technology

publications.title: Green Internet of Things (IoT) with dynamic sleep wake-up approach for constrained things
publications.abstract: Energy consumption has now become a big deal to ensure the dependability of the IoT. Therefore, minimization of energy consumption is the biggest challenge in IoT architecture. IoT devices are supported with constrained parameters like battery, memory as well as computing. This paper gives a depth analysis of battery-powered things and their green implementation with dynamic Sleep, Wake-up approach based on a decision-making process supported by highly specified data analysis. The proposed method is based on an Energy-Efficient Cluster Head-Based Sleep Scheduling Mechanism (ECHSSM) for efficient Sleep, Wake-up monitoring with dynamic changes in time duration. The architectural prototype for the application scenario for humidity and temperature is studied. The implementation of the model is done by the Cooja simulator. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is examined using some parameters, such as the lifetime of the network, packet delivery ratio, energy consumption, battery level, and delay characteristic. The proposed technique improves the network lifetime by 11.95%, 7.59%, and 3.83% better than EEHC, LEACH, and cloud-IoT integrated models.

publications.title: Image processing and pattern recognition-based car classification for intelligent transportation system
publications.abstract: The combination of car model classification and accelerated advances in computer vision appears to have the potential to significantly revolutionize automated transportation systems. Pattern recognition and image processing-based car classification methods have been proposed in recent years to improve the performance of smart highway toll collection and monitoring of traffic systems. Unfortunately, all these algorithms are trained on a inadequate number of features derived from tiny datasets, which do not considered for real-time road traffic circumstances. To address these difficulties, proposed system presents a classification model for vehicle based on convolutional neural networks to enhance the resilience of car classifier model in real-time applications. To achieve real-time robustness in classification systems, this proposed system offers a Stanford car dataset of 16,185 images classified into 157 common vehicle classes. To begin, the car dataset was trained using Inception-v3, VGG16, and ResNet50 to evaluate their accuracy based on performance. As a result, a comparative study was carried out to assess the effectiveness of the proposed system.

publications.title: An Efficient Deep Learning Model with Optimization Techniques for Lung Disease Detection
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Computational Robotics, Testing and Engineering Evaluation (ICCRTEE)
publications.abstract: Lung diseases have been a leading cause of morbidity in the world hence the need to have smart systems to aid in early identification and monitoring of the risks. It provides a Hybrid Digital Twin Lung AI Framework to detect hierarchical lung disease and provide AI-assisted clinical decision support using the Exasens dataset in the UCI Machine Learning (ML) Repository. The proposed model will combine XGBoost as the main classifier, a lightweight Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) to complementary learn, and K-Means-based phenotype clustering to improve feature representation. The optimization of hyperparameters is done through Optuna-based techniques in order to enhance robustness and generalization. Probability calibration and adaptive threshold tuning provide severity-aware classification. In addition to prediction, a digital twin-inspired module also allows monitoring risks in real-time, medication safety, and warning about critical conditions. The framework also embraces adaptive medication reminder programs and systematic self-care practices to enhance treatment compliance and to reduce the possible risks of medication. Stratified crossvalidation performance is 75.02 % accurate, 73.89 % F1-score, 0.8808 % AUC, and 0.9003 % Average Precision. The suggested multidisciplinary model brings the traditional classifiers to the risk-conscious clinical decision ecosystem that can be scaled.
publications.publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers

publications.title: Optimized Deep Learning Framework for Blood Cancer Diagnosis
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Computational Robotics, Testing and Engineering Evaluation (ICCRTEE)
publications.abstract: Blood cancer continues to be a major health problem in the world and its early detection. Blood cancer is one of the major health issues facing the world and its early detection is the only way of guaranteeing that more patients will survive. Nevertheless, it is hard to diagnose early in high-dimensional data of molecular profiling because of non-balanced cohorts, manual feature engineering, and non-optimized Deep Learning (DL) models that restrain generalization and clinical usage. The suggested DuTCN-QNet is the refined DL architecture, which is to be applied to detect leukemia based on microarray gene expression data. The AI model combines an Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) and Dual CNN-TCN architecture, which allows the efficient selection of features and Quantum-Inspired Swarm Optimization (QSO) to optimize the hyperparameters automatically. The framework makes use of a publicly repository dataset provided by PLOS Figshare (S1 Dataset of HDG-select) and does controlled jitter-based augmentation to augment its robustness. To improve reliability and interpretability, calibrated confidence, accuracy, F1-score, recall, precision, as well as SHAPbased quantitative explanation are used to perform performance evaluation. The results of the experiment prove that DuTCNQNet can reach a higher detection accuracy, better calibration and high generalization on unknown samples. Moreover, the measures of evaluation are contrasted to the current state of art methods using proposed model. The suggested framework is valuable to be deployed in practice in pathology processes, tele-health risk assessment, portable diagnostic equipment, and population-wide screening programs of leukemia, facilitating accessible and scalable early detection algorithms globally.

publications.title: Hybrid Deep Learning for Voice-Activated Pre-Order System Using DistilBERT
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on AI-Driven Innovations & Applications (IC-AIDA)
publications.abstract: This paper presents the enhancement of efficiency and user experience through development of a food pre ordering application for university’s cafeterias and shops. This application leverages Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning which further supports voice-based ordering with existing models like DistilBERT and Google’s speech libraries. Also, Sentimental analysis of the users improves the suggestions and quality of services, while LSTM based demand forecasting reduces food wastage. This provides insights on inventory, customer feedbacks and as well as inventory. On Each Order, the application generates a unique QR code which keep track of the proper order time, pickup and the ingredients used. The application supports UN Sustainable goals i.e SDG 9 by promoting the digital innovation in the food ordering platforms SDG 11 by enhancing sustainable urban food distribution and SDG12 by reducing the food wastage. The application is designed in such a way that it is user friendly, secure, and easy to adapt, making it a meaningful platform and tool for digitizing campus food and beverage services.
publications.publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers

publications.title: A Deep Learning Based Approach for Data Security and Error Detection in Massive IoT-CPS Systems
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development
publications.abstract: The emergence of artificial intelligence and machine learning (AIML) enabled high speed wireless networks has culminated in the practical conceptualization of cyber physical systems (CPS). 5 G and 6 G enabled software defined networks have become a key enabler for large Internet of Things (IoT) and fog networks allowing communication between massive numbers of heterogeneous devices. However, massive heterogeneous CPS are prone to cyber-attacks along with lack of trustworthiness due to diverse and sophisticated cyber-attacks along with communication errors for mobile and vehicular networks. The purpose of the study is to develop a deep learning based approach which, based on the channel response can identify potential adversarial attacks on the network. The methodology developed in this paper leverages the channel state information and deep learning for data security as well as error minimization. Moreover, a separate deep learning model is developed with mimics the recursive Bahl Coche Jalenik Raviv (BCJR) decoding algorithm employed to convolutional and turbo codes. The Deep Learning enabled encoder-decoder structure is shown to perform well in the presence of Gaussian Noise conditions and attains bit error rates (BER) of$\text{1 0 - 5}$at SNR of 0.5 dB while outperforming contemporary baseline approaches. The bidirectional Long Short Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) model is employed for stochastic feature training for data authentication against security attacks. It has been shown that the model attains an average accuracy of 0.995 against jamming and injection attacks beating or performing at least at par with contemporary Deep Learning algorithms. Thus the proposed approach serves both purposes of securing wireless network and CPS as well as enhancing the reliability of data sharing in CPS, based on an accurate deep learning based error detection and correction mechanism.

publications.title: A Deep Learning–Enabled Computer Vision System for Real-Time Tomato Spider Mite Detection
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Intelligent Computing, Networks, and Security (IC-ICNS)
publications.abstract: Tomato spider mite disorder is a problem which affects the heath of the tomatoes and is due to the mite Tetranychus urticae. The mite at first affects the leaf and causes its surface to have yellowish/whitish patches and the effect of the mite feeding at last cause pale/bronze patches. The disorder on becoming more damaging results in leaf falling and curling. The areas under the leaf are also damaged and webs are formed. The growth of the leaves is also inhibited. The photosynthesis also reduces and the fruits come out as bad. The mite flourishes in hot/humid weather and disorder causes market loss. To inhibit the growth of mite which is difficult in open areas the farmers use the chemicals, removal of infected leaves and natural predators. Due to these reasons the early detection of the disorder inhibits the issue. This work uses a GoogLeNet based model on an online dataset. The performance-metric attained by this work is very efficient and results in the accuracy of 100 percent which is perfect. This model in short is efficient, simple and can help farmers get the work done.
publications.publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers

publications.title: PhishGuard: A Hybrid NLP-Computer Vision Approach for Real-Time Phishing Detection in a Browser Extension
publications.journalOrConferenceName: IEEE International Conference for Convergence in Computing Technology (I3CTCON)
publications.abstract: Some less traditional methods for observing phishing attacks have relied on blacklists or other singular dimensions using increasingly complex attacks. To this end, this paper introduces Phish Guard, a novel Chrome browser extension designed for state-of-the-art detection of fake and fraudulent websites in real time. Unlike existing systems, this one has a hybrid approach by synergistically using Natural Language Processing (NLP) to analyze the browser-created textual content and Computer Vision (CV) to detect deceptive visual layouts and brand impersonation. This dual-modal system provides a strong defense mechanism that analyzes both website languages and website forms simultaneously. This method looks at the glaring need for a more comprehensive and client-side detection tool that can very effectively detect and neutralize zero-day phishing threats, consequently increasing user safety. Evaluation of the hybrid model against the traditional detection paradigms is done.
publications.publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers

publications.title: Optimization-Guided Deep Learning and Blockchain Framework for Secure Smart EV Charging Systems
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Advancement in Futuristic Technologies (ICAFT)
publications.abstract: The charging networks of electric vehicles (EV) need to operate securely, adaptively, and with low latency in order to handle changing demands in the modern smart-mobility context. It introduces an AI architecture built on the GT-Boost-NSGA Scheduler and integrating the real-time load forecasting, priority-based charging coordination, and blockchain-based secure payment systems. The integrated pipeline Natural Gradient Boosting (NGBoost) is a Graph Transformer Network, the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III) and forecasts the demand of charging, runs a computational analyzing plan, and authenticates energy transactions by using tamper-resistant smart-contract execution. A global comparative analysis is carried out to determine the performance in relation to the existing means, and it can be seen that there has been a measurable increase in the performance of the system in terms of transactional security, charging performance, and reliability. Temporal charging log experiments, geospatial station attributes, and blockchain transaction records demonstrate a total accuracy of 97.52%, fewer overloads occurrences and lower authentication latency when compared to the baseline solutions. The system enhances the decision-making process with such selective threat notification, which only received validated anomalies are forwarded to charging operators, fleet management hubs, control.
publications.publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers

publications.title: AI-Driven Brain Stroke Detection with Outcome-Optimized Triage and Alerts
publications.abstract: Brain stroke is a sudden cranial vascular condition that demands quick and outcome-focused medical care. This work presents an AI-based framework that combines early stroke detection, subtype classification, and hospital selection support for use in prehospital and emergency settings. The framework uses a hybrid pipeline, XGB-CNNBi-LSTM-CMAES (DT-Lite Triage), which first identifies stroke versus non-stroke cases, then separates ischemic and hemorrhagic types, and finally recommends treatment centers by considering past hospital outcomes and travel-time estimates. Experiments on the California Hospital Inpatient Mortality and Quality Ratings dataset with geospatial data report an overall accuracy of$99.00 \%(0.990017)$and fewer false negatives compared to existing methods, while aligning hospital referrals with outcome-based rankings. At the last stage, the system extends detection to survival-focused alerts, sending timely notifications to hospitals, ambulance services, and emergency teams; these alerts are fewer than early detections, showing selective escalation. A comparative evaluation with existing approaches highlights improved results, stronger reliability, and clear clinical value of the proposed framework for stroke decision-making across diverse scenarios in healthcare.

publications.title: AI-Driven Prediction of Silent Heart Attacks and Cardiac Events in Real Time
publications.abstract: Silent cardiac events, including silent heart attacks, cardiac arrests, and septal defects, often remain undetected due to the absence of symptoms and delays in manual assessments, resulting in life-threatening conditions. This paper presents a novel AI-driven detection framework, HGS-CNN-TabNet + XGBoost, for the real-time prediction of critical cardiac events using continuous ECG monitoring. The framework extracts multimodal ECG and patient features through a hybrid ensemble architecture that integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for spatial ECG pattern analysis and TabNet for processing patient metadata. Hunger Games Search (HGS) optimizes feature selection and hyperparameters, while XGBoost performs the final classification into safe, moderate, and critical risk categories. The proposed framework incorporates an IoT-based instant emergency alert mechanism that automatically notifies families, doctors, hospitals, and ambulance services during high-risk episodes, enabling golden-time intervention within the first few minutes. Experimental outcomes achieves 99.75 % high prediction accuracy with consistent evaluation metrics. Comparative analysis with existing approaches demonstrates improved detection performance and reduced false negatives, highlighting the potential of the proposed framework to support timely clinical decision-making.
affiliation: University Institute of Engineering Chandigarh University

publications.title: Dynamic Music Recommender Based on User Mood and Affect Using Machine Learning
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Innovations and Emerging Technologies in AI & Communication Systems (IETACS)
publications.abstract: Music has always been a part of human civilization since ancient times. It not only greatly influences human emotions, but it is also proven that it can influence cognitive function, physical health, and even social behaviour. These benefits as well as overall user experience can greatly be enhanced with the combination of music and artificial intelligence. The surge of music streaming platforms like Spotify, Gaana, You Tube Music, etc. ends up frequently overwhelming the users with its extensive music libraries, which in turn ends up complicating the process of choosing songs that actually match their current feelings and fit their vibe. Traditional music recommendation systems that are mostly dependent on content-based or collaborative filtering often struggling with a cold start and a lack of proper emotional context. To address such issues, this study presents a better dynamic music suggestion system that specifically generates a tailored song recommendation by recognizing the users emotions in real-time. This system uses certain methods such as machine learning and computer vision, to assess and thoroughly understand the user's facial expression, eventually detecting user's emotions as well by utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for feature extraction. The InceptionV3 architecture has been utilized to obtain and detect facial features, which is later on categorized using machine learning methods such as Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Logistic Regression. This system bridges emotional intelligence with personalized music experiences. The system recognizes the users emotions, and the recognized user's emotion is then associated with a thoughtfully designed music playlist provided through a hybrid recommendation method that merges the content-based filtering with emotion based sensitive context.
publications.publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers

publications.title: AI-Powered Optimization in Vertical Farming: Predicting Crop Yield Using Environmental Parameters
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
publications.abstract: Increasing demand for sustainable agricultural practices has driven the adoption of controlled-environment agriculture, such as vertical farming. In this study, we propose an AI-powered approach to optimize crop yield prediction using environmental parameters within vertical farming systems. A publicly available dataset from Kaggle was used, containing over 36,000 records of environmental conditions and corresponding crop yields. After preprocessing and feature engineering, several regression models were evaluated, including Linear Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost. Among them, XGBoost achieved the best performance with an R2 score of 0.9776 and RMSE of 3.99. To ensure model interpretability, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was applied, revealing key environmental features that influence yield outcomes. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of machine learning models-especially XGBoost-when combined with explainable AI techniques for precision agriculture and offers a reliable framework for real-time yield forecasting in vertical farming systems. Our novel contribution lies in demonstrating the synergistic power of advanced machine learning (XGBoost) and Explainable AI (SHAP) to not only achieve unprecedented predictive accuracy in vertical farming but, more critically, to demystify the ‘black box’ and provide actionable, interpretable insights for real-time environmental control, a gap largely unaddressed in existing literature.

publications.title: AI-Powered Plant Disease Detection Using EfficientNetB3 with Deep Learning
publications.journalOrConferenceName: IEEE Uttar Pradesh Section Women in Engineering International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Engineering (UPWIECON)
publications.abstract: Accurate detection of plant diseases is crucial for stable crop production in India, where agriculture remains the primary economic engine. Significant yield losses often result from inaccurate or delayed diagnoses, directly affecting farmers' livelihoods and the nation's agricultural output. To address this issue, there is a growing need for scientific and technologically advanced approaches. Automated plant disease detection systems can benefit farmers by reducing manual labour, lowering the risk of crop failure, and promoting higher productivity and economic sustainability. This work bridges existing research gaps and address limitations in current approaches in plant disease detection strategy. Our system is trained on diverse datasets using EfficientNetB3 with deep learning for accurate and early leaf disease detection with an overall accuracy of 99.7%. Through multiple training cycles, the model's performance is enhanced to serve as an effective, scalable, and consistent tool for assisting farmers in achieving better crop health and sustainable agricultural outcomes.
publications.publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers

publications.title: An AI Based Multimodal System for Understanding and Answering Questions Using Mistral 7B
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
publications.abstract: Data is a collection of raw facts, figures, or details that, when processed, become meaningful information.” The special quality of the data is that it is considered a wealth of utmost significance in the technical world. The proposed AI-based multimodal system ensures this level of significance by maintaining data integrity and confidentiality for the same. This model is designed in such a way that it can take input from the user through text or can use a microphone to take commands from the end user. The system grips AI models for real-time document parsing, contextual question answering, and semantic analysis. The output of the device is that it uses advanced technology to answer user questions by finding important points from these documents in the formatted form of PDFs, URLs, and YouTube videos. It highlights the required information with page or slide numbers, making it easy to locate the information with accuracy and precision, resulting in a productive outcome by consuming a short time for the end-user.

publications.title: Beyond Depression: A Two-Phase Framework for Comorbid Anxiety Detection in Depressed Individuals Using Transcript-Based Emotional and Semantic Features
publications.journalOrConferenceName: IEEE Uttar Pradesh Section Women in Engineering International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Engineering (UPWIECON)
publications.abstract: In today's world, anxiety and depression have become ubiquitous, affecting large number of populations worldwide. Although a considerable amount of work has been done on automatic detection of these mental health problems individually but comorbid detection of anxiety in depressed individuals still remains underexplored. This study proposes a two-phase framework for the comorbid detection of anxiety in depressed individuals. In Phase 1, it uses lexical features, affective indicators derived from Empath lexicon, and sentence level embeddings generated by a pre-trained transformer model for diagnosing depression and in Phase 2, anxiety is diagnosed in subset of depressed individuals by employing a pseudo-labelling strategy grounded in emotion features and clinical comorbidity rates from STAR*D study. Accuracy and F1 score metrics were used for evaluating the models. Results from Phase 1 were considerably moderate with F1 score of 0.64 for the depression detection, while Phase 2 showed significantly stronger performance by achieving F1 score of 0.97 for anxiety detection using a voting-based ensemble classifier. The models of both phases are trained by using the DAIC-WOZ dataset and focus solely on transcript-based features to ensure its applicability in resource constrained environments. These findings clearly depict the effectiveness of emotion-focused features and percentile-based thresholding in detecting the comorbid anxiety in the subset of depressed individuals. Overall, from this study we can see that transcript-based models can offer scalable, low-cost and interpretable solutions for comorbid mental health screenings and it also lays the foundation for then future multimodal or multi-task learning approaches in comorbid mental health assessment.
publications.publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers

publications.title: Predictive Analytics for Reducing Post-Harvest Losses in Agriculture
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Computing Applications (ICCICA)
publications.abstract: Postharvest losses in agriculture are a major challenge to food security, the economic viability of agriculture, and sustainable agricultural practices all over the globe. Any losses in quantity and quality of an agricultural produce that occur between harvest and consumption are deemed postharvest losses; and these constitute a serious challenge, especially in most developing nations. This study investigates the possible application of predictive analytics as a game changer in minimizing postharvest losses by allowing data-driven decisions along the agricultural value chain. Predictive models will assess environmental parameters in real-time supplemented by historical data on the crops and supply chain metrics to assess spoilage risk, thus optimizing storage and transport environments and timely market interventions. The study utilizes machine learning algorithms such as regression analysis, decision trees, and also time series forecasting in developing models that can predict probable loss scenarios for selected key crops; this data will include satellite imagery, weather data, storage facility records, and also the marketing trends. Results from the predictive models are measured in terms of accuracy, scalability, and usability for farmers, cooperatives, and policymakers. The research further discusses data availability, integration across heterogeneous systems, and the injustice presented to smallholder farmers due to the digital literacy divide. The results indicate that predictive analytics can plug in an early warning and actionable insight so that stakeholders can act before any spoilage occurs, which significantly brings down post-harvest losses. Some case studies from selected regions have demonstrated improvements in storage planning, supply chain coordination, and post-harvest handling practices. The paper concludes with recommendations for integrating predictive tools with agricultural extension systems and policies at the state level with due consideration for capacity building, development of digital infrastructure, and partnership with the private sector. The ultimate expectation is that predictive analytics can therefore allow for increased resilience, efficiency, and sustainability within the agricultural system.

publications.title: AI-Powered Fraud Detection in Real-Time IoT-Enabled Payment Systems
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference for Advancement in Technology (ICONAT)
publications.abstract: Existing fraud detection systems often rely on static datasets and neglect real-time IoT-based contextual information, limiting their adaptability to dynamic transaction environments. Fraudulent activity is frequently detected post-transaction, delaying response measures and increasing user exposure to financial risks. Moreover, the absence of an integrated framework for tracing fraud origins and escalating incidents to legal authorities hampers effective threat mitigation. The study introduces hybrid Artificial Intelligence (AI) architecture that incorporates Black Hole Optimization (BHO) for optimal feature subset selection, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for hierarchical feature representation, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) for high-precision classification. The framework processes both transactional and device-level attributes to enable context-aware, real-time fraud detection. Comparative evaluations against existing approaches reveal substantial gains in detection accuracy, responsiveness, and mitigation efficiency. Experimental findings demonstrate that the proposed BHO-CNN+XGBoost model attains overall accuracy of 99.03% and a Stratified 5-Fold CrossValidation accuracy of 99.14%, surpassing conventional baselines. The system facilitates instantaneous alerts, fraudster geo-location tracing, automated cybercrime reporting, and device blocking, offering a lightweight, deployment-ready solution for IoT-enabled payment infrastructures and services worldwide in practice.

publications.title: Optimized Hybrid Learning for Alzheimer's Detection and Medication Compliance
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference for Advancement in Technology (ICONAT)
publications.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is developing neurological condition that impairs memory, cognition, behavior. Timely diagnosis and intervention play a vital role in improving clinical outcomes and enhancing patient quality of life. This study introduces an optimization-guided hybrid framework that integrates Contracted Fox Optimization (CFO), Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU), and Random Forest (RF) for early AD detection utilising publicly available multimodal dataset from kaggle. The proposed model initially detects the presence of Alzheimer's and subsequently classifies patients based on medication compliance. For non-compliant individuals, an AI-driven reminder mechanism activates to support treatment adherence. The CFO+BiGRU+RF model achieves an accuracy of 97.40%, significantly outperforming state-of-the art classifiers include Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, and Decision Tree. Additionally, the proposed framework is evaluated against a baseline model, demonstrating improved performance and robustness using standard metrics. This framework facilitates early detection, compliance prediction, and intelligent intervention, offering strong potential for deployment in clinical healthcare environments for Alzheimer's management and care improvement efforts.

publications.title: IAS and Facial Recognition System
publications.abstract: In this chapter of the book, the intricate relationships between intelligent automation systems (IASs) and facial recognition systems—two cutting-edge technologies that are transforming the domains of automation and biometric identification—are examined. IAS and facial recognition technology together provide unparalleled convenience, security, and efficiency for a variety of uses. The chapter begins with an introduction to IASs, outlining their basic components and demonstrating how they make of robotic process automation, artificial intelligence, and machine learning to streamline complex operations. After that, it delves into the theoretical underpinnings of face recognition technology, elucidating the underlying algorithms, potential applications, and ethical considerations. The bulk of the chapter looks at how IAS and facial recognition systems integrate, showing real-world applications in a range of sectors like banking, retail, healthcare, and security. However, the chapter also addresses the challenges and ethical considerations surrounding the integration of IAS and face recognition. A thorough examination of privacy concerns is followed by a discussion of the importance of ethical and legal frameworks for risk reduction. The latter sections of the chapter look at potential directions for further study and the integration of face recognition.

publications.title: Computer Vision and Deep Learning for Early Detection of Target Spot in Tomato Plants
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Computing and Communications (COMPUTINGCON)
publications.abstract: Tomato Target Spot which caused by the fungal pathogen Corynespora cassiicola severely impacts the plant health and also leads to the significant yield losses. The disease initially appears as the small, the dark brown to black circular lesions with concentric rings on the leaves, the stems and the fruits. Also the favorable conditions allow these lesions to expand and coalesce causing the extensive necrosis, the yellowing and the premature defoliation. In the severe cases the infection spreads rapidly thereby weakening the plant and also reducing the fruit quality and the productivity. The targetspot also thrives in the warm and humid environments that particularly when prolonged allow for leaf wetness which occurs due to the rain, the high humidity or the overhead irrigation. The farmers manage the target-spot through the resistant cultivars, the proper field sanitation, the crop rotation and the optimal plant spacing to improve the airflow. The fungicides may also be applied preventively during the highrisk periods. This study proposes the deep-learning based classifier to automatically distinguish between the healthy tomato leaves and those infected with target-spot. The input images undergo preprocessing to enhance the contrast and retain the critical-disease features. A fine-tuned GoogLeNet architecture is trained on an augmented dataset and effectively identifies the disease markers such as the lesion morphology, the concentric ring patterns and the necrotic tissue. The model achieves a classification accuracy of 92.97 % demonstrating its potential for the early disease detection. The results highlight the viability of deep-learning in enabling the precisionagriculture providing the farmers with a tool for timely intervention and improved crop-monitoring systems. The future work includes integrating this model into the mobile and drone-based systems for real-time field diagnostics.

publications.journalOrConferenceName: Global Conference on Information Technology and Communication Networks (GITCON)
publications.abstract: Anxiety is psychological disorder that affects individuals both mentally and physically, often causing emotional stress, sleep issues, and behavioral changes. Early detection of anxiety can help prevent long-term mental health problems. The current research presents Machine Learning (ML) strategy utilised for identifying whether person is experiencing anxiety by utilizing physiological information (includes heart rate and EEG) along with behavioral data (includes sleep patterns and phone usage). Several hybrid models is developed and tested, including SVM+CNN, RF+CNN, XGBoost+CNN, GA+CNN, and PSO+CNN. The PSO+CNN model attained superior accuracy of 99.35%. The proposed model is evaluated against traditional methods to assess performance. The proposed model is lightweight and real-time anxiety detection in practical applications for emotional health support for emotional health support and improved user experience outcomes and strategies.

publications.title: The Early Classification of Diabetes using Machine Learning
publications.abstract: Diabetes is everywhere, and if not caught early, it can quickly turn into serious health problems. The use of machine learning based model on a mix of clinical attributes to figure out who might be diabetic is a good option. This research involves use of seven different models for spot checking which are Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbors, Gradient Boosting, Decision Tree, Naive Bayes and Random Forest. The Random Forest ended up at the front with about 74.8% accuracy. The clinical feature importances were checked using three algorithms Gradient Boosting, Logistic Regression and Random Forest. This extra layer of insight not only helped with predictions but also made it a bit easier to understand what is really driving the diabetes detection efforts. Overall, the study points to a promising direction for early diabetes detection using machine learning with Random Forest clearly taking the lead. The recurring appearance of certain clinical indicators underlines, in its own way, which factors truly matter, it’s a small, yet meaningful, step towards smarter healthcare that might one day assist in clinical diagnoses and lead to more personalized treatment strategies.

publications.title: E-Voting Using Blockchain
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
publications.abstract: Abstract: Democratic rule is based on safe and open electoral systems that can preserve their authenticity. The conventional voting processes are hampered significantly by electoral fraud and security breaches as well as centralized management and inefficiencies in auditability and accessibility. The issues of electoral systems reduce public trust along with lowering the credibility of election results. This paper introduces a new three-tier blockchain-based e-voting system designed to enhance voter privacy alongside system scalability and end-to-end verifiability to restore trust in electoral processes. Voter verification at Layer 1 (Identity Verification) combines Decentralized Identity (DID) with Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKP) and multimodal biometric techniques involving fingerprint scanning, facial recognition technology, and voice analysis. The system enables only the participation of valid voters while also protecting their private data and fulfilling different user needs. The system's Layer 2 (Vote Casting & Secure Storage) employs a hybrid consensus algorithm combining Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) and Delegated Proof-of-Stake (dPoS) to store votes securely while reducing energy consumption. The system leverages Triple-Blind Signatures to provide complete voter anonymity by decoupling voter identities from their votes as well as any accompanying metadata. Lattice-based post-quantum cryptography is employed to encrypt votes which are distributed across sharded blockchain subnets for enhanced performance without sacrificing fault tolerance. The system accumulates votes via Merkle roots and verifies them via zk-SNARKs in Layer 3 (Result Processing & Transparency) that allows public observation without compromising voter privacy. A Live Audit Dashboard provides voters with the capability to check their vote in real time which facilitates transparent and accountable voting processes. The suggested system attains a secure and open electronic voting process using sophisticated cryptographic protocols in a decentralized setup compliant with international requirements while enabling digital democratic participation.

A Deep Neural Network Model for Forecasting Variable Stock Movement Intervals
publications.abstract: Forecasting results for stock markets exhibit variabilities in forecasting accuracy as the tenure of prediction is varied. Typically stocks are predicted for long, short as well as mid term tenures based on the tenure of prediction. While longer tenures have relatively much larger data to be trained as training data, divergences are also potentially large as the forecasting period may render higher randomness due to unprecedented events. The short term forecasting is relatively less prone to unprecedented events due to the tenure of forecasting. However, the lesser amount of training data may result in less accurate pattern recognition. A common ground is typically found in terms of mid term forecasting. This paper presents an experimental evaluation of all three formats of forecasting based on the training, testing split. The deep neural network model is used for the forecasting purpose and the forecasting MAPE and accuracy has been tabulated for a multitude of stocks. It has been shown that the proposed approach attains an MAPE of only 2.18% outperforming existing work in the domain.

Finance applications currently are heavily reliant of data driven models. Stock trend analysis happens to be one such approach, which lays the foundation for forecasting decisions to be made. The leeway in such applications is critically small as minimal inaccuracies in forecasting may lead to major losses. This paper presents the current perspective in terms of evolutionary algorithms such as artificial intelligence and Blockchain and how they are transforming software development, the application of machine learning algorithms to regression problems. publications.title: An Efficient CNN Autoencoder Framework with Adaptive Thresholding for Video Anomaly Detection in Intelligent Surveillance Systems
publications.abstract: Video anomaly detection can also be considered another concept that holds significant importance in developing an intelligent surveillance system because of its capability to detect anomalies automatically. In a traditional surveillance system, the degree of dependence on manual surveillance is very high; in fact, this type of system is both costly and error-prone. Although there are various applications of deep learning methods for detecting anomalies in videos, they show bad results regarding the generalization performance and generate many false positives. To overcome these challenges, this work presents a novel implementation of an efficient reconstruction-based CNN Autoencoder framework that includes batch normalization, dropout regularization, data augmentation and adaptive thresholding. These adjustments help in improving generalization and reducing false alarms. In this research paper, CNN Autoencoder is proposed to detect video anomaly by reconstruction loss. This method is tested using two widely adopted benchmark datasets: UCSD Ped1 and UCSD Ped2. The approach is basically a combination of various techniques, including CNN layers, batch normalization, dropouts, learning rate tuning, and the adaptive thresholding technique. Our model gives an ROC-AUC score of 98.32% for the Ped1 and 99.32% for the Ped2 dataset. Moreover, our proposed approach gives a 98.67% accuracy, 100% precision, 98.63% recall, and 99.31% F1-score for the Ped2 dataset.

publications.title: Attention-Enhanced Deep Learning Framework for Breast Cancer Detection Using Histopathological Images
publications.abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most prevalent and deadly of all diseases among women globally. Computer-aided diagnosis enables accurate and timely classification of breast tissue, improving treatment outcomes. Despite its significant achievement in medical image classification, class imbalance, poor feature representation and lacking interoperability remain concerns that limit model performance in the medical image classification task. In this study, an architecture of deep learning with attention is proposed for breast cancer classification based on histopathological images. The proposed model is based on the EfficientNetV2-S backbone network with the addition of a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to learn discriminative features across different channel-wise and spatial representations. Minority classes will benefit from the reduction of the effect of class imbalance through the use of Focal Loss in the training phase. The model is tested with the benign and malignant breast tissue images included in the BreakHis dataset, which is publicly available. Experimental results show that the proposed approach provides better classification results with accuracy of 98.17%, precision of 98.91%, recall of 98.38%, F1-score of 98.64% and AUC-ROC of 0.9985. An ablation study also verifies that the attention mechanism and imbalance-aware optimization make a big difference to the predictive performance. The results obtained from these findings suggest that the proposed method is a reliable and efficient approach for automated breast cancer diagnosis and can help assist pathologists to take quicker and more precise medical decisions.

publications.title: Cardio-Detect: A Hybrid ML-DL Technique for Identifying Cardiovascular Diseases in ECG Images
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
publications.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide. Early and accurate detection is critical to reducing the risk of fatal outcomes. Electrocardiogram (ECG) analysis is a fundamental diagnostic tool used to detect abnormalities associated with myocardial infarction (MI), arrhythmias, and other cardiac conditions. However, manual interpretation of ECGs is time-consuming, susceptible to human error, and requires specialized expertise, highlighting the need for automated diagnostic methods. While deep neural networks (DNNs) offer high accuracy, they often require extensive computational resources, which can hinder real-time deployment. On the other hand, traditional machine learning (ML) approaches struggle to manage the complex patterns inherent in ECG image data.Our model is trained on a diverse dataset comprising ECG images from four categories: patients with myocardial infarction, individuals with a history of MI, those with arrhythmias, and subjects with normal heart rhythms. This comprehensive dataset ensures broad representation of various cardiac conditions. Feature extraction is performed using EfficientNetB0, a lightweight yet powerful convolutional neural network. The model achieves a training accuracy of 91.26%, with improved generalization capabilities attributed to effective preprocessing and data augmentation strategies. By leveraging the efficient feature extraction capabilities of EfficientNetB0 and coupling it with a simple yet effective machine-learned classifier, our model offers a scalable and computationally economical solution for ECG image analysis. This approach facilitates accurate, timely, and accessible cardiovascular disease detection.

publications.title: Enhanced Cyber Phishing Website Detection using a Stacked Classifier Combining ML and DL
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Data Communication Systems (ICSCDS)
publications.abstract: Phishing, a prevalent cyberattack, deceives individuals into disclosing sensitive details or installing malware. Initially executed via email, phishing attacks have expanded to text messages, phone calls, and social media. Despite cybersecurity advancements, phishing remains a major threat, with 3.4 billion phishing emails sent daily. In response, we propose a hybrid stacked classifier combining ML and DL models for phishing website detection. The first layer includes Random Forest and Decision Tree, while the second layer integrates Multi-Layer Perceptron and XGBoost. The model achieves a test accuracy of 97.38%, precision of 97.14%, recall of 98.10%, and an F1 score of 97.62%. Performance is further validated by ROC analysis, demonstrating its effectiveness in minimizing false positives and maximizing true positive rates. This approach offers a robust, scalable solution for phishing detection, with potential for real-time application optimization.

publications.title: Sparse Coding Techniques with Deep Neural Network for EEG Auto Encoding: Enhancing Feature Representation Efficiency
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Recent Advances in Information Technology
publications.abstract: Research on emotion classification using Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) systems is an intriguing aspect. Deep learning has recently been used to classify emotions in BCI systems, and better results have been seen when compared to more conventional classification techniques. Although the high dimensionality and noise of Electroencephalography (EEG) signals make it difficult to research brain activity is essential for efficient feature representation. To improve the effectiveness of feature representation, describe a unique method in this paper for EEG autoencoding that combines Sparse Coding Techniques with Deep Neural Networks (SCT-DNN).. Using several encoding and decoding layers, the deep auto-encoder is intended to learn hierarchical representations that capture crucial aspects of the EEG signal. Promote efficient representation and reconstruction of EEG signals by enticing the machine to learn sparse and discriminative features through the use of sparse coding throughout the encoding phase. Results from the experiment demonstrate the advantages of SCT-DNN for learning EEG features and provide insights into the underlying brain processes. Through the synergistic use of deep learning and sparse coding, this proposed work optimizes the efficiency of feature representation, furthering the field of EEG signal analysis.

publications.title: Unveiling Emitter Trends in Heavy Duty Vehicles using Extreme Gradient Boosting algorithm
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Recent Advances in Information Technology
publications.abstract: The increasing use of Heavy-Duty Vehicles (HDV) has spurred the development of advanced techniques for analyzing and forecasting emission patterns. In this study, researchers present a novel method using the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm to identify emission patterns in HDV. A sophisticated prediction model was constructed using a large dataset encompassing various vehicle aspects, such as engine specifications, operating conditions, and pollution levels. The XGBoost algorithm extracts intricate nonlinear correlations from the data, providing significant insights into emission patterns. The proposed model demonstrates improved precision in prediction and generalization capabilities through cross-validation and comparison with traditional predictive methods. The findings highlight crucial factors influencing emissions that benefit public and private stakeholders in mitigating environmental impact. This study showcases XGBoost’s ecological statistical capabilities and sets a foundation for future advancements in robust vehicle emission trend analysis.

publications.title: Advanced Anomaly Detection in Cloud Security Using Gini Impurity and ML
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Applied Artificial Intelligence and Computing (ICAAIC)
publications.abstract: Cloud security research has shown significant advances in terms of anomaly detection, with attention on cloud security. For instance, autoencoders were used to improve anomaly detection in cloud networks indicating that these methods can outperform traditional ones. In comparison with previous techniques, the proposed technique differs from them in the way it calculates reconstruction error; determines the appropriate thresholds and compares these errors against the thresholding method. In this research, grid search is used to tune model parameters and performance evaluations were then carried out using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, false positive rate and F1 score on CIDDS-001 dataset. Findings show that this could be a highly efficient approach for developing autoencoder-based IDS systems.

publications.title: Automating the Detection of Road Damage via the Use of UAV-Captured Images and the YOLO
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Smart Electronics and Communication (ICOSEC)
publications.abstract: This research introduces an interesting methodology for the automated recognition of road damage employing images captured by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and the YOLO (You Only Look Once) Deep Learning (DL) algorithm. Although conventional road inspection techniques are risky and wasteful, maintaining a reliable road network is essential to public safety and economic growth. This work utilizes UAVs to capture high-resolution images of road surfaces, which are subsequently analyzed using YOLOv5, YOLOv7, and the latest YOLOv8 models. Through comprehensive training and testing, including data augmentation techniques, models in this work are fine-tuned for high accuracy in road damage detection. The results demonstrate that YOLOv8 achieves the highest accuracy, significantly outperforming earlier versions. This study underscores the ability to integrate UAV technology with DL for efficient, accurate, and scalable road maintenance solutions.

publications.title: Early knee osteoarthritis classification using distributed explainable convolutional neural network with local interpretable model-agnostic explanations
publications.abstract: Abstract Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA) is a type of Knee Arthritis (KA) that causes pain, swelling, and other discomforts to the knee joints, which is quite complicated to classify using previous methods due to its various limitations such as computational cost, over-fitting issues, less reliability and so on. In this research, the classification using a distributed explainable convolutional neural network with local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LExNN) model is proposed for knee Osteoarthritis. The distributed LExNN model is an ensemble with a distributed mechanism, in which the input vectors are distributed to two explainable CNNs which makes it quite easier for classification and grading. The distributed concepts are blown up with several advantages such as high computation efficiency with less training time, reliability, and develop an efficient model for classification. In addition, the local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME) technique interprets important information from the image and classifies the severity based on two grades namely high and low. This technique provides significant, simple, and understandable information, which is quite reliable for KOA classification. The supremacy of the model can be determined by measuring several parameters such as accuracy, precision, recall, and f1 score that gives 99.25%, 99.25%, 98.42%, and 98.83% compared to other state-of-the-art methods.

publications.title: Innovative Integration of Deep Learning and Neural Networks in Heart Disease Prediction
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Computational Intelligence for Security, Communication and Sustainable Development (CISCSD)
publications.abstract: Globally, one of the leading causes of mortality is heart disease, necessitating timely along with accurate detection to enhance the results for patients. In the following paper, a generalized approach to heart disease detection using deep learning is introduced with the view to finding means of utilizing the most cutting-edge machine learning techniques to improve cardiovascular healthcare. The main focus of academic inquiry is directed at utilizing deep learning algorithms to analyze a multitude and variety of medical data, including electrocardiogram images, in order to discover the most effective and precise technique of early heart disease detection and diagnosis. Thus, in this study, a wide range of highly popular state-of-the-art inside deep learning architectures were considered, including but not limited to the neural networks with convolutions. Moreover, the scholars had carefully analyzed and compared above-mentioned architectures using their own method to determine the most suitable one for the detection of cardiac conditions. In the current study, the author applied ECG and electrocardiogram images as their dataset had more varied electrocardiogram images. The dataset's diversity enables the models to capture intricate patterns and achieve robust generalization, essential for real-world deployment. These experimental results demonstrate promising potential for improving heart disease diagnosis and risk assessment, showcasing significantly enhanced performance compared to conventional methods. The study emphasizes the importance of early diagnosis of cardiac disorders in improving patient outcomes and treatment planning. In conclusion, this work provides a thorough investigation of a broad deep learning method for detecting heart disease. By combining diverse medical data, advanced deep learning architectures, and model training techniques, the research showcases the potential of artificial intelligence in revolutionizing cardiovascular healthcare. To anticipate that the findings will inspire future research and applications in the medical domain, leading to enhanced early diagnosis and improved patient care.
