publications.title: An Environmental Sustainable Approach to Machine Learning, Training and Development
publications.journalOrConferenceName: Sakarya University Journal of Computer and Information Sciences
publications.abstract: Artificial intelligence has the potential to drive sustainability by minimizing the impact of machine learning (ML) development on the environment. However, many ML techniques, particularly ensemble methods like the Random Forest classifier, require large computational resources during the tuning of hyperparameters. These hyperparameters are the number of trees, the depth of the tree, and the number of features considered at each split of the tree. These hyperparameters considerably impact model performance and energy consumption. This paper proposes an eco-friendly multi-objective framework (EFMOF) to optimize the hyperparameters with minimal environmental impact while retaining high model accuracy. By leveraging advanced hyperparameter optimization techniques like Optuna, Hyperopt, and Grid Search, the framework effectively explores the hyperparameter space, focusing on energy efficiency and carbon reduction. From the above, incorporating sustainable AI into ML development requires monitoring energy consumption and carbon emissions at every hyperparameter tuning. This will ensure that the models developed perform well and are sustainable without too much environmental cost. The Experimental result shows that the most dominant hyperparameter is the number of estimators, which leads to higher energy consumption. In contrast, minimum samples per leaf and split have a moderate effect, while maximum depth has a minor impact.

publications.title: Green AI Practices in Multi-objective Hyperparameter Optimization for Sustainable Machine Learning
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Journal of Information Technology and Computer Science
publications.abstract: The hyperparameter tuning process is an essential step for ML model optimization, as it is necessary to improve model performance. However, this enhancement involves high computational resources and time costs. Model tuning can significantly raise energy consumption and consequently increase carbon emissions. Therefore, there is an essential need to construct a new framework for this challenge by adding carbon emissions as a vital consideration along with performance. The paper proposes a novel Sustainable Hyperparameter Optimization (SHPO) framework that uses an optimized multi-objective fitness approach. The framework focuses on ensemble classification models (ECMs) namely, Random Forest, ExtraTrees, XGBoost, and AdaBoost. All these models will be optimized using traditional and advanced techniques like Optuna, Hyperopt, and Grid Search. The proposed framework tracks carbon emissions during model hyperparameter tuning. The methodology uses the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) as a method of multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM). This TOPSIS method ranks the hyperparameter sets based on both accuracy and carbon emissions. The objective of the multi-objective fitness approach is to reach the best parameter set with high accuracy and low carbon emissions. It is observed from the experimental results that Optuna based Hyperparameter optimization consistently produced low carbon emissions and achieved high predictive accuracy across the majority of benchmark hyperparameter setups for the models.

publications.title: Minimizing the Carbon Footprint of Machine Learning Techniques through Sustainable AI Training Methods
publications.journalOrConferenceName: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series
publications.abstract: The increasing development and deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) systems add to the environmental impact concerns. Machine learning training requires huge amounts of energy for training large-scale models, particularly deep learning networks in a data center which is in most cases built by non-renewable energy sources. As AI applications expand, their energy demands grow, exacerbating their contribution to global carbon emissions and climate change. Several approaches (such as optimized algorithms, energy-efficient hardware, renewable energy infrastructure, green data centers, and advanced cooling techniques) have emerged to mitigate the carbon footprint associated with the AI development pipeline. This chapter proposes a novel algorithm carbon-aware pso-based hyperparameter optimization (HPO) that incorporates a dual-objective function, where the aim is to maximize model accuracy while minimizing carbon emissions. Unlike traditional HPO methods, the proposed algorithm integrates early stopping to cut off unnecessary computation which significantly reduces training time with less energy consumption. The algorithm is executed on energy-efficient hardware configurations, including CPUs and GPUs, to leverage hardware-specific advantages and optimize resource usage. The algorithm balances both software-level optimizations like early stopping and hardware acceleration in showing an approach toward making ML eco-friendly, thus meeting the needs for both model performance and environmental efficiency. This approach addresses the dual challenges of high model performance and environmental impact, contributing to a sustainable future in the AI development scenario. This algorithm holds immense potential for future deployment in renewable energy infrastructure cloud platforms to achieve significant carbon reduction and adopt an eco-friendly environment. This alignment with renewable energy infrastructures represents a transformative step toward reducing AI's environmental impact and achieving long-term goals for sustainable technological innovation.

publications.title: Optimized Stacking Ensemble Classifier for Early Cancer Detection Using Biomarker Data
publications.journalOrConferenceName: Advance Sustainable Science Engineering and Technology
publications.abstract: Ovarian cancer ranks sixth globally as a major cause of death among women, with a five-year survival rate below 50%, largely due to late detection. Early detection is crucial to lower mortality rates. This paper introduces an Optimized Stacking Ensemble Classifier (OSEC) for early ovarian cancer detection using biomarkers. The model comprises two layers: the first layer includes base classifiers optimized with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), while the second layer is a meta-classifier integrating Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), and Random Forest(RF) models fine-tuned through grid search. Among the three datasets evaluated, the Blood Routine dataset showed the best performance with a stacked RF meta-classifier, achieving: 94.29% accuracy. The Stacked RF model also outperformed others, reaching 92.82% accuracy on the Serum dataset and 92.77% on the Malignant Ovarian Tumor (MOT) dataset, consistently excelling in precision, recall, and f1-score.

publications.title: Fusion Learning of Regression Models for Missing Data Imputation in Breast Cancer Dataset
publications.journalOrConferenceName: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
publications.abstract: Regression-based imputation techniques are successful for the collective work of missing data imputation in data preparation. However, these methods may not perform well when faced with multi-pattern missing data. This learning proposes a Fusion Learning approach namely a competitive ensemble of regression models that combine the predictions of multiple regression models to improve the accuracy of multi-pattern missing data imputation in the Breast Cancer dataset. The proposed method involves generating multiple subsets of the data using different random seeds and training a regression model on each subset. The trained models are then fused using a simple averaging approach. Our experiments show that the Fusion Learning methodology achieves higher imputation accuracy than numerous advanced imputation techniques, especially when the missing data patterns are difficult. The results suggest that Fusion Learning of Regression Models can be an effective approach for multi-pattern missing data imputation in the Breast Cancer dataset.

publications.title: Enhancing Federated Learning in Healthcare Using Adaptive Genetic Model Aggregation
publications.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a new paradigm for collaborative training of machine learning (ML) models without sharing sensitive data, thus making it highly relevant in privacy-critical domains such as healthcare. This chapter focuses on the application of FL to breast cancer (BC) classification, which is a challenging task in healthcare that requires accurate predictive models. This chapter introduces an innovative adaptive genetic aggregation (AGA) algorithm that enhances the aggregation process in FL. The data distribution is heterogeneous across clients. The AGA uses evolutionary principles, adaptive crossover mechanisms, and mutation mechanisms to determine the performances of the global model. This approach selects and aggregates the best-performing local models regarding efficient update integration from a wide range of clients dynamically. The performance of the AGA algorithm was evaluated on the BC dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach can reach an accuracy of 98.5% on the final run. Hence, the proposed method outperforms the traditional aggregation techniques, including FedAvg, FedProx, and FedSAM, both in terms of accuracy, convergence speed, and communication cost.

publications.title: Metric number theory of Fourier coefficients of Hilbert modular forms
publications.abstract: In this paper, we attempt to generalize the work of Bengoechea (2019) to the case of Hilbert cusp forms. We prove Diophantine approximation of a real number by Fourier coefficients (supported at prime powers) of a primitive Hilbert cusp forms and we compute the density of such prime ideals. We also study the refined rate of approximation of real numbers by Fourier coefficients of primitive Hilbert cusp forms, using techniques and results from metric number theory such as Schmidt’s game and metrical inhomogeneous Diophantine approximation.
